title: Schwamendingen Dorfplatz pocket forest, stormwater & solar hub for families and seniors
description: Transform Schwamendingen Dorfplatz (near Kirche Schwamendingen and Bus stop Schwamendingen) into a 30‑tree pocket forest with 6 rain‑gardens, two 120 m3 cisterns for stormwater capture, 20 solar‑charging benches, native pollinator plantings and a playable water feature. Target groups: families, older residents, school classes (Schwamendinger Schulhaus visits) and small businesses. Implementation: co‑design workshops (6 weeks), construction in phases to keep plaza usable, 18‑month timeline, ongoing community stewardship program and sensor monitoring for soil moisture and overflow alerts.

title: Saatlen–Hirzenbach green roof & solar retrofit for 50 buildings, tenants & schools
description: District‑scale retrofit: subsidise and install vegetated roofs + rooftop PV on 50 multi‑family houses across Saatlen and Hirzenbach, with pilot installations at Schulhaus Saatlen and Seniorenzentrum Schwamendingen. Deliver insulation upgrades, biodiversity modules, rainwater retention trays and tenant education. Includes a 30‑person local training/apprenticeship program for retrofit works, digital dashboard for energy/water savings, and a 36‑month rollout with maintenance contracts. Benefits: reduced runoff, lower heating costs for tenants, new green habitat corridors and local green jobs.

title: Schwamendingen–Stettbach Rapid Bus Corridor: Dedicated e‑bus lanes and smart stops
description: Create a 2.8–3.5 km dedicated rapid bus corridor from Schwamendingenplatz to Stettbach S‑Bahn (via Schwamendingenstrasse/Saatlen), with raised boarding platforms at 6 stops (Schwamendingenplatz, Hirzenbach, Saatlen, Geissweid, two intermediate stops), electric articulated buses, traffic‑signal priority, realtime displays, covered solar bus shelters and integrated protected cycle lanes. Targets commuters, students and seniors. Implementation: planning 6 months, construction/phasing 18–30 months, full operation by year 3. Expected benefits: travel time cut 30–50%, fewer local car trips, better connections to Stettbach and city centre.

title: Schwamendingenplatz Car‑free Plaza and Multimodal Hub for Kreis 12 Residents
description: Transform Schwamendingenplatz into a car‑reduced, accessible multimodal plaza: covered bus/tram terminal island, widened pedestrian&cycle boulevards, rain gardens and play pocket parks, 4 neighbourhood mobility hubs (Schwamendingen Mitte, Saatlen, Hirzenbach, Geissweid) offering secure bike parking, e‑cargo bike share, charging lockers and a community repair workshop. Includes smart wayfinding, single app for booking/payments and accessibility ramps. Timeline: design 6–9 months, staged works 12–24 months. Beneficiaries: families, elderly, schoolchildren, local retailers — creates safe public centre and hub for sustainable trips across Kreis 12.

title: Dübendorfstrasse–Schwamendingen Green Mobility Corridor and Quartier Hubs for Residents
description: Transform 1.2 km of Dübendorfstrasse from Schwamendingen Zentrum to Hirzenbach/Stettbach with protected bike lanes, widened pavements, bioswale street greenery and three mini “Quartier Hubs” (Schwamendingen Zentrum market square, Bachtel-/Dübendorfstrasse corner, near Hirzenbach bus stop). Hubs offer community rooms, childcare pop-ups, a tool library, community fridge, coworking space, solar charging benches, smart lighting and air-quality sensors. Targets families, commuters, seniors and youth. Implementation: 3-year phased plan—Year 1 design & pilots with Primarschule and Seniorenheim, Year 2 build lanes & green infrastructure, Year 3 install smart tech and launch programs.

title: Schwamendingen Smart Clean Corridor on Dübendorfstrasse for Residents & Commuters
description: Create a smart-clean corridor from Schwamendingenplatz along Dübendorfstrasse to Saatlenpark: 30 solar compacting sensor bins, two community micro-hubs (Schwamendingenplatz, Saatlenpark) for sorting, tool-lending and education, an electric night-sweeper route using sensor-driven dynamic routing, rapid-response graffiti/illegal dumping team, and a neighbourhood app with maps and reward points. Targets residents, shops, commuters and schools. Timeline: 3 months planning, 6 months procurement/install, 12–18 month pilot with quarterly evaluations and local volunteer clean-days.

title: Kreis 12 Safe Night: Smart Lighting + 3 Community Safety Hubs in Schwamendingen, Saatlen, Hirzenbach
description: Install 120 adaptive LED streetlights with motion, noise and air sensors along Schwamendingen Bahnhof–Waldgarten corridor; build three staffed safety hubs (near Schwamendingen Bahnhof, Saatlenpark playground, Zürich Hirzenbach Haltestelle) with CCTV feed access for Stadtpolizei, AED, heated waiting area and lockable safe room. Target groups: elderly, youth, evening commuters. Implementation: pilot at Schwamendingen Bahnhof (months 1–6), full lighting roll-out and hubs (months 6–18), police/volunteer training and community outreach (months 3–24). Integrate data with Zürich smart-city dashboard; maintain for 5 years.

title: Schwamendingenplatz Intergenerational Makerspace & Cultural Lab for Youth and Seniors
description: Convert vacant municipal rooms at Schwamendingenplatz (adjacent to the bus/tram interchange) into a staffed makerspace and cultural lab for youth, seniors, migrants and local artists. Fit-out: 3D printers/CNC, podcast/recording booth, rehearsal room, multilingual theatre classroom and drop-in IT helpdesk. Program: intergenerational workshops with Primarschule Schwamendingen, evening performances, job-skills bootcamps. Governance: community board with quotas for residents. Timeline: 18 months (6 months planning/community design, 9 months renovation/equipment, 3 months pilot).

title: Saatlen–Hirzenbach Cultural Green Corridor and Smart Festival Route
description: Create a linear cultural park from Saatlen Park through Schwamendingenplatz to Hirzenbach Siedlung: pocket amphitheatres, solar streetlighting, smart benches, free Wi‑Fi, waste & bike hubs and AR multilingual history/stories plaques (DE/EN/AL/SR). Install removable market infrastructure for weekend pop-ups and a yearly 3‑day ‘KulturTage Kreis 12’ anchored at Schwamendingenplatz and Hirzenbach community hall to boost local vendors and performers. Target: residents, commuters, small businesses. Timeline: 30 months phased (6 months design, 12 months pilots, 12 months full rollout).

title: Schwamendingen STEAM Youth Hub at Dorfplatz — Makerspace, Mentoring, Tutoring
description: Convert a vacant municipal hall at Schwamendingen Dorfplatz into a free STEAM Youth Hub (ages 10–18). Install a digital fabrication lab (3D printers, laser cutter, CNC), coding & robotics labs, sound booth, study & tutoring rooms, and apprenticeship coaching in partnership with Schulhaus Schwamendingen and Jugendtreff. Add rooftop solar, smart-booking kiosks, and multilingual workshops for migrant families. Timeline: 18 months — 3 months co-design, 9 months renovation & equipment, 6 months pilot; ongoing school integration and weekend community programs.

title: Smart Fitness Trail from Bahnhof Altstetten to Albisrieden — Free Training for Residents
description: Install a 1.8 km inclusive outdoor fitness and mobility trail linking Bahnhof Altstetten (west exit) along Limmattalstrasse to Schulanlage Albisrieden. Ten solar-lit exercise stations (low-impact, senior-friendly, calisthenics, balance) with multilingual QR-video tutorials (DE/EN/AL/IT), wayfinding, seating and repair stations. Target groups: commuters, school classes, seniors, migrant families. Timeline: 3 months planning, 6 months procurement, 6–9 months installation, community launch. Partners: Sportamt Zürich, Quartierverein Altstetten/Albisrieden, local schools. Smart sensors measure use; free public classes in first year.

title: Climate-Positive Altstetten Sports Campus at West Bahnhof Altstetten — Pools & Halls
description: Transform the disused SBB lot west of Bahnhof Altstetten (adjacent to Limmattalstrasse) into a climate-positive indoor sports campus: 25m public pool with learn-to-swim classrooms, divisible multisport hall, rooftop synthetic turf small pitch, public skate plaza and a physiotherapy & vocational training hub for sports careers. Smart booking app reserves school slots (Schulanlage Albisrieden), community rehab, and discounted hours for seniors and refugees. Timeline: 6m feasibility, 6m design/permits, 18–24m construction. Sustainability: PV, geothermal heating, rainwater harvesting. Funding: city + canton + federal sport grants + local partners.

title: Schwamendingenplatz Modular Co‑Housing: Affordable Intergenerational Homes & Social Hub
description: Transform three municipal surface parking lots along Schaffhauserstrasse between Schwamendingenplatz tram stop and Ruggacherstrasse into 80 energy‑plus modular apartments (studios–3‑room), plus ground‑floor childcare, shared kitchens, a health/social services office, rooftop community gardens, and a zero‑emission mobility hub at Schwamendingenplatz. Retrofit adjacent block Däumlistrasse 5–9 to add 20 co‑living units. Smart building management, resident app for services, and phased 36‑month timeline. Targets low‑income families, seniors, young adults, and refugees; financed by PB, city housing funds, and cantonal subsidy.

title: Schwamendingen Mitte Community Health & Telecare Hub for Seniors, Families, Migrants
description: Repurpose vacant retail next to Schwamendingen Mitte bus/tram hub (near Gemeindezentrum Schwamendingen) into an integrated Health & Telecare Hub. Services: walk‑in primary care, multilingual health navigators, mental‑health drop‑in, physiotherapy studio, community nutrition kitchen, telemedicine booths linked to Stadtspital and UZH, wearable‑loan library, and a therapeutic pocket garden. Target groups: seniors, migrant families, low‑income and youth. Timeline: 0–6 months co‑design with neighbourhood, 6–18 months retrofit and staffing, open months 18–24 with evaluation year 2.

title: Kreis 12 Oerlikon Jobs & Green‑Tech Training Hub at Bahnhof Oerlikon
description: Convert vacant municipal premises beside Bahnhof Oerlikon (near Hallenstadion/Messe Zürich) into a Jobs & Green‑Tech Training Hub for Kreis 12 residents. Target groups: unemployed locals, youth 16–25, migrants, women returning to work and small businesses. Deliverables: 30 co‑working desks, 8 maker/repair bays, 20‑place childcare, solar/EV retrofitting workshop, IT/coding lab, pop‑up hiring space linking to Messe Zürich. Timeline: planning 0–6 months, renovation 6–18 months, pilot programs and app-based micro‑internships 18–24 months. Partners: Stadt Zürich, RAV, local employers, Messe Zürich.

title: Altstetten–Albisriederplatz Green Corridor: Urban Wetland, Shade & Sensors for Residents
description: Transform Limmattalstrasse corridor between Bahnhof Zürich Altstetten and Albisriederplatz (~1.2 km) into a climate‑resilient green spine: bioswales and permeable paving to cut runoff, three stormwater attenuation pockets/mini‑wetlands, 320 native trees and shaded seating, three pocket parks with play elements, protected cycle lane enhancements, and an IoT sensor network (soil moisture, air temp) feeding a public dashboard. Targets families, elderly, commuters and cyclists. Timeline: design 3 months, permits 3 months, construction/planting 9 months, first‑year monitoring.

title: Bahnhof Altstetten Solar-Biodiversity Roof Hub: Energy, Workshops, Pollinators for Neighbours
description: Convert the rooftop of the Bahnhof Zürich Altstetten parking structure and adjacent pedestrian overpass into a Community Solar & Biodiversity Hub: 350–450 kWp PV array with ~200 kWh battery, green‑roof pollinator meadows, rainwater harvesting for irrigation, two EV chargers, 100 m² modular workshop/classroom for school and neighbourhood programmes, and community microplots. Benefits commuters, local schools, small businesses and residents. Partners: SBB, Stadt Zürich, local Vereine. Timeline: feasibility 3 months, permits 3 months, installation 9 months, programming launch 6 months.

title: Bahnhofplatz Altstetten Zero‑Emission Mobility Hub: Velostation, e‑fleet and green community plaza
description: Transform Bahnhofplatz Altstetten into an integrated mobility hub (SBB/VBZ/Limmattalbahn interface). Deliver a 400‑space secure velostation with 80 e‑charging docks, 10 public e‑cargo bikes, a 30‑vehicle shared electric minibus fleet for last‑mile service, dedicated bus/tram priority lanes, and a planted green roof plaza with seating and local market stalls. Target: commuters, students, seniors and local shops. Timeline: planning 6 months, construction 24 months. Partners: Stadt Zürich, SBB, VBZ, Limmattalbahn, local businesses. Expected effect: modal shift, less car parking pressure, inclusive access.

title: Albisriederplatz–Bahnhof Altstetten Protected Active‑Travel Corridor with smart crossings
description: Create a continuous protected cycle and pedestrian corridor along Albisriederstrasse from Albisriederplatz to Bahnhof Altstetten: two segregated bike lanes, widened sidewalks, raised zebra crossings with vibration/LED alerts and bus signal priority. Add 3 heated winter pilot blocks, 2 neighbourhood cargo‑bike libraries, secure micro‑mobility parking, wayfinding to schools and Pflegeheim locations, and a community engagement programme for schools and elderly. Timeline: design 6 months, phased delivery 12–18 months. Benefits: safer school routes, increased active travel, reduced traffic noise and stronger local commerce.

title: Badenerstrasse–Albisriederplatz Green Spine: Active Car‑Light Corridor for Altstetten & Albisrieden
description: Transform Badenerstrasse (Bahnhof Altstetten plaza to Albisriederplatz) into a 750‑m car‑light ‘green spine’: remove one traffic lane, add a protected 3 m bidirectional cycleway, widened sidewalks, six pocket parks/play nodes, rain gardens and permeable paving. Install solar pergolas and smart benches with Wi‑Fi/USB at tram stops (Albisriederplatz, Bahnhof Altstetten), secure cargo‑bike hub (30 stalls) and real‑time air‑quality sensors. Target: families, commuters, elderly, local businesses. Timeline: 6 months participatory design, 6 months technical approvals, 12 months phased construction plus ongoing community stewardship programs.

title: Smart Clean Corridor: Badenerstrasse — Bahnhof Altstetten to Albisriederplatz for residents & commuters
description: Pilot an 18‑month clean-streets corridor along Badenerstrasse between Bahnhof Altstetten and Albisriederplatz: install 20 solar smart bins (fill+odor sensors), 10 motion-activated anti-graffiti cameras at SBB underpasses and tram stops, two e-cargo bikes for nightly micro-collections, and a neighbourhood “Clean Hub” at the Altstetten plaza. Target groups: commuters, local shops, families, elderly. Goals: 50% less litter, graffiti removals within 48h. Timeline: 3 months planning, 3 months install, 12 months operation with monthly community clean-ups and data dashboard for Stadt Zürich.

title: Smart Safe Corridor on Badenerstrasse (Bahnhof Altstetten–Albisriederplatz) for residents & commuters
description: Transform Badenerstrasse (Bahnhof Altstetten to Albisriederplatz) into a 'Smart Safe Corridor' for residents, commuters, night-shift workers and businesses: adaptive LED lighting (20 poles), 8 emergency call pillars, 12 privacy-by-design AI cameras for anomaly alerts, pedestrian- and cycle-priority crossings, a community safety hub at Freilager Zürich offering staffed night-time Safety Ambassadors and co-response teams with Sozialdepartement/Zürcher Polizei. Phased 24-month rollout: 6-month planning, 12-month pilot, 6-month scale, plus public dashboard, app alerts, and community oversight.

title: Herti Creative Commons: Digital Maker & Performing Arts Hub at Bahnhof Altstetten
description: Convert a 1,200–1,500 m² vacant hall in the Herti‑Areal (walking distance from Bahnhof Altstetten) into co‑working studios, soundproof rehearsal rooms (4), a 200‑seat flexible black‑box theatre, digital fabrication lab (3D printers, CNC), AR/recording booth and subsidised residency spaces. Targets youth, immigrant artists, seniors and school groups. Implementation: 6 months design & community workshops, 12 months renovation, launch in month 19. Features app booking, real‑time occupancy sensors and solar rooftop panels.

title: Badenerstrasse Cultural Boulevard: Open‑Air Stage, Night Market, Micro‑Galleries
description: Transform the Badenerstrasse stretch between Albisriederplatz and Bahnhof Altstetten into a pedestrian cultural boulevard: widened sidewalks, one central 250 m² modular amphitheatre at Albisriederplatz, 10 lockable micro‑gallery kiosks, curated mural program, and biweekly night market supporting local vendors. Targets families, commuters, small businesses and multicultural groups. Timeline: 6 months planning & traffic study, 3 months pilot car‑free weekends, 18 months phased construction, full rollout month 28. Integrates smart lighting, public Wi‑Fi and tram access continuity.

title: Freilager–Bahnhof Altstetten Youth STEAM & Apprenticeship Hub for 10–19-year-olds
description: Transform vacant Freilager rooms and the Bahnhof Zürich Altstetten plaza into a youth STEAM & apprenticeship hub for Altstetten/Albisrieden residents (ages 10–19). Install maker labs (3D printers, CNC, textiles), a rooftop classroom and climate garden at Freilager, a sheltered pop-up learning pod on Badenerstrasse by the station, and a mobile learning van visiting Schulhaus Albisrieden. Provide an app for bookings, IoT/AR kits, evening apprenticeship matchmaking nights with local firms. Timeline: 6‑month pilot, full roll-out in 24 months. Target: ~500 participants/year, ~40 apprenticeship matches.

title: Smart Sports Campus at Schulhaus Albisrieden — inclusive courts for youth & seniors
description: Create a modular multi-sports campus on the triangular public space between Schulhaus Albisrieden, Badenerstrasse and Albisriederstrasse (near Bahnhof Altstetten). Install hybrid turf courts, solar LED smart lighting, sensor-enabled fitness stations, a community climbing wall and rooftop basketball court on the school gym. Add accessible changing rooms, locker hub and weekly coached programmes for youth (6–18), seniors and disability sports. Implementation: design 6 months, build 12 months, partners: Stadt Zürich Sportamt, local Vereine, schools; 18-month total timeline.

title: Limmat Water‑Sports & Active Greenway from Bahnhof Altstetten to Albisriederstrasse
description: Transform the Limmat embankment by Bahnhof Altstetten into a 1.2 km active greenway with separated running/cycling lanes, flood‑resilient floating dock, community boathouse for kayaks/SUPs, adaptive-boat storage, repair station, showers and lockers. Integrate smart booking/learning app, sensor lighting, and a calendar of school programmes and annual neighbourhood regatta. Target groups: families, schools, sports clubs and commuters. Implementation: planning & permits 9 months, construction & commissioning 21 months; managed by local sports associations and Stadt Zürich.

title: Energy-positive intergenerational co-housing at Badenerstrasse near Bahnhof Altstetten
description: Replace the municipal surface parking strip south of Bahnhof Altstetten along Badenerstrasse with ~80 modular apartments (35% permanently affordable), ground-floor childcare and community kitchen, on-site social-service office for refugees and low-income households, rooftop urban farm and PV, district heat-pump and battery storage, secure bike hub. Target groups: seniors, young families, essential workers, newly arrived refugees. Timeline: 6 months feasibility, 12 months design/permits, 18 months construction; community cooperative governance and phased occupancy in year 3.

title: Altstetten Viaduct Commons: Intercultural Hub, Workshop & Solar Garden at Bahnhof Altstetten
description: Transform the unused SBB viaduct space beside Bahnhof Altstetten (Badenerstrasse / Schärenmoosstrasse entrance) into a 600 m² community hub for Albisrieden/Altstetten residents: 30‑seat communal kitchen, repair‑café and makerspace with 4 workshop bays, digital skills lab (15 workstations), intergenerational daycare pop‑up, and a 120 m² rooftop/community solar garden powering LED lighting, free Wi‑Fi and EV cargo‑bike charging. Target groups: migrants, unemployed youth, seniors, families. Timeline: design & permits 6 months, build 12 months, pilot programs 6 months. Governance: resident council and partner NGOs for programming.

title: Bahnhof Altstetten Community Health Hub and Green Rehab for Seniors, Youth, Migrants
description: Repurpose vacant retail/office space beside Bahnhof Altstetten into a single-site primary-care clinic, mental‑health counselling, physiotherapy studio and telemedicine booths; add a therapeutic pocket garden on Albisriederplatz and mobile e-health van serving Albisrieden senior homes. Targets seniors, commuters, migrants and low‑income families. Features multilingual digital triage kiosks, air‑quality & noise sensors, integrated appointment system with Stadt Zürich eHealth. Timeline: 0–6 months planning & partnerships (Stadt, Spitäler), 6–18 months retrofit & pilot, 18–36 months scale-up and neighbourhood outreach.

title: Bahnhof Altstetten Green Jobs & Maker Campus for Badenerstrasse Residents
description: Convert vacant retail units along Badenerstrasse (east side of Zürich Altstetten station) and an underused SBB-side service hall into a Green Jobs & Maker Campus. Offer digital fabrication (CNC, 3D print, textile lab), e-mobility repair bays with cargo-bike fleet, and a local hiring/skills platform. Target: unemployed youth, migrants, micro-entrepreneurs. Deliverables: 30 paid 6–12 month apprenticeships per year, workspace for 40 microbusinesses, monthly Altstetten Makers Market on the station forecourt. Timeline: planning 0–6m, buildout 6–18m, program launch 18–24m.

title: Limmatquai Living Shoreline: Floating Wetlands and Sensors (Rathausbrücke–Bürkliplatz)
description: Install 30 modular floating-wetland platforms anchored along Limmatquai between Rathausbrücke and Bürkliplatz, each 2×5 m with native reeds, seating, low-glare LED lighting and IoT water-quality/temperature sensors. Targets: Kreis 1 residents, schools, seniors and cafés. Benefits: cooler microclimate, improved water quality, biodiversity corridors and community learning. Implementation: site survey and permissions 3 months, build and anchor 6 months, community monitoring programme with UZH and local schools for 3 months (total 12 months). Volunteers stewarding and quarterly maintenance included.

title: Bahnhofstrasse–Bellevue Green Roof & Solar Network with Community Food Hubs
description: Retrofit eight city-owned rooftops between Bahnhofstrasse and Bellevue (including Bahnhofplatz and Bürkliplatz parking roofs and Stadthaus roof) with 600 m² extensive green roofs, 500 kWp PV, 300 kWh battery storage, rainwater tanks and 20 community garden plots + urban beehives. Targets: local renters, elderly, neighbourhood associations and commuters. Benefits: heat reduction, local renewable power for streetlights and 10 EV chargers, food production, apprenticeships. Implementation: structural surveys 3 months, reinforcement 9 months, green/PV installation 9 months, community handover and training 3 months (24 months total).

title: Bellevue Underground Secure Bike Hub & Cargo-Bike Library for Kreis 1 Residents
description: Convert the underpass/garage area beneath Bellevueplatz (adjacent to Bellevue tram stop and the opera/Sechseläutenplatz edge) into a 24/7 secure bike garage (≈800 spaces) plus a 30-unit community cargo-bike library, staffed repair bench and e-bike charging. Target: residents, parents, seniors, small businesses. Access via ZürichPass app, priority resident subscriptions and low-income discounts. Timeline: design 6 months, construction 12–18 months, soft-launch at 20 months. Integrate real-time occupancy API for VBZ journey planners.

title: Limmatquai Active Corridor: Pedestrian-first Boulevard with Tram Priority and Micro-Logistics Hub
description: Pilot pedestrian-first Limmatquai between Rathausbrücke and Bellevue: raised shared surfaces, widened footpaths, green seating pockets by Grossmünster and Münsterbrücke, adaptive tram-priority signals, AR wayfinding to Bahnhofstrasse/Paradeplatz, and weekend car-free programming. Create a consolidated electric micro-logistics depot at Bürkliplatz for last-mile deliveries with e-trikes and timed delivery windows to cut van traffic. Timeline: 6-month pilot (partial closure), 18-month redesign, 6-month evaluation. Benefits residents, elderly, retailers, schools and cuts noise and emissions.

title: Altstadt Micro‑Hub Network: 5 Community Hubs for Residents across Lindenhof, Niederdorf, Bellevue, Bürkliplatz, Bahnhofstrasse
description: Transform five precise sites into resident-first micro‑hubs: Lindenhof terrace (community kitchen + elder check‑in), Niederdorf/Helmhaus alley (childcare pop‑up + cultural stage), Bellevue stair landing (co‑working pods + public Wi‑Fi), Bürkliplatz tram edge (bike repair + parcel lockers), Bahnhofstrasse side street near Rennweg (local startup incubator + meeting room). Retrofit empty kiosks/parking bays, add smart benches with solar charging, air‑quality sensors, rain gardens and monthly neighbourhood programming. Target: Kreis 1 residents (seniors, families, freelancers). Implementation: 6‑month planning, 12‑month roll‑out, 6‑month evaluation. Partners: Stadt Zürich, Quartierverein, ZVV, local landlords.

title: Smart Clean Streets Hub: Bahnhofstrasse–Niederdorf Litter-Free Corridors for Residents and Shops
description: Pilot a Smart Clean Streets system in Kreis 1: 12 solar compacting IoT bins (Bahnhofplatz→Paradeplatz, Limmatquai from Grossmünster to Rathausbrücke, Niederdorfstrasse, Bellevue), two e‑bike rapid‑clean crews for night/weekend shifts, dog‑waste & recycling micro‑hubs at Bürkliplatz and Bürkliterrasse, plus footfall and fill‑level sensors feeding a public dashboard. Partner with Stadt Zürich Reinigung, local shops and NGOs. Timeline: months 1–3 permits/procurement, 4–6 installation/training, 7–12 pilot & evaluation. Targets: −40% litter pickups, −80% bin overflows.

title: Smart Night Safety Corridor: Bahnhofstrasse–Limmatquai for Residents, Elderly, Night Workers
description: Create a Smart Night Safety Corridor covering Bahnhofstrasse (Bürkliplatz–Paradeplatz), Limmatquai (Münsterbrücke–Bellevue) and Niederdorfstrasse: 20 sensor-LED poles with anonymized edge analytics, 4 staffed Night Safety Pods (Bellevue, Bürkliplatz, Paradeplatz, Central) offering first aid/cooling/info, 30 trained community safety stewards patrolling 19:00–03:00, 12 new AEDs, upgraded zebra crossings and tram-stop lighting. Targets Kreis 1 residents (particularly elderly), night workers and families. Timeline: 3 months planning/community oversight, 9 months pilot, 6 months full rollout. Integrated with Stadtpolizei dispatch, clear privacy rules and local resident governance.

title: Limmat Cultural Corridor: Interactive Art Trail from Bahnhofbrücke to Münsterbrücke for Residents
description: Transform Limmatquai between Bahnhofbrücke and Münsterbrücke into a year‑round cultural corridor: smart LED lighting, AR historical guided routes (Grossmünster/Fraumünster stops), retractable micro‑stages at Lindenhof and Stadthausquai, free public Wi‑Fi, smart benches with charging, and a resident artist residency program. Target groups: Kreis 1 residents, local schools, senior centres, and artists. Implementation: phased 18‑month rollout with pilot pop‑ups (6 months), permanent installations (months 7–18) and partnership with Kunsthaus Zürich and local Quartierverein for programming.

title: Floating Limmat Stage at Bürkliplatz: Community Boat Venue for Local Artists and Seniors
description: Refurbish a decommissioned Limmatboat docked at Bürkliplatz/Münsterquai into a year‑round, accessible community stage and workshop space offering intergenerational programming (music, theatre, oral history) for Kreis 1 residents. Improvements: soundproofing, wheelchair lift, modular stage, rehearsal studios, community-run box office, and scheduled school and senior sessions. Timeline: feasibility & permits 6 months, refit 9–12 months, launch festival at 18 months. Operations managed by a municipal‑seeded cooperative with hourly community booking and discounted resident tickets.

title: Urania STEAM & Arts Youth Hub for Kreis 1 (Uraniastrasse, Bellevue)
description: Convert Urania Sternwarte (Uraniastrasse 9, Bellevue) basement and mezzanine into a free STEAM + arts hub for 10–18 year olds living in Kreis 1. Fit-out: FabLab (6×3D printers, laser cutter, CNC), robotics/VR lab, sound booth and theatre-technical workshop. Offer after-school tutoring, bilingual mentorship, apprenticeships with Kunsthaus Zürich and Opernhaus Zürich, and summer internships with Bahnhofstrasse retailers. Pop-up weekend maker festivals on Sechseläutenplatz and learning benches at Bürkliplatz. Timeline: 3 months design/permits, 9 months build, pilot program launch month 13.

title: Bürkliplatz Limmat Floating Aquatic Hub: Accessible Swim, SUP, Kayak for Kreis 1 Residents
description: Install a modular pontoon complex anchored at Stadthausquai/Bürkliplatz (by the Bürkliplatz tram stop) with 50m swim lanes, wheelchair ramps, SUP/kayak launch, lifeguard station, and pop-up changing/storage containers on the quay. Add real-time water-quality sensors and a booking app for lessons, community swims and club storage. Target: families, commuters, students, people with reduced mobility. Implementation: Hafenmeister/Tiefbau permits, 12–18 months, seasonal lifeguards, volunteer training program and school outreach starting month 6.

title: Sechseläuten Smart Sports Pavilion: All-Weather Courts & Programs for youth, seniors, families
description: Create a retractable, all-weather sports pavilion on Sechseläutenplatz (adjacent Schauspielhaus / Bellevue tram stop) with configurable courts (basketball, futsal, badminton), heated non-slip surface, LED lighting, climbing boulder, lockers and smart booking/occupancy sensors. Offer scheduled intergenerational classes, school partnerships, senior movement sessions and weekend tournament events. Implementation: design with Grün Stadt Zürich and Stadt Zürich Denkmalpflege, modular construction to preserve plaza, 18–24 months, phased community programming rollout and local clubs’ use agreements.

title: Convert Upper Floors along Bahnhofstrasse–Limmatquai into Modular Affordable Co‑Housing for Kreis 1 Residents
description: Adaptive reuse of upper floors of mixed‑use buildings between Bürkliplatz and Central (Bahnhofstrasse/Limmatquai, incl. areas near Bellevue and Stadelhofen) into 60–80 modular micro‑apartments and 10 intergenerational family units. Targets young families, seniors, single parents, local artists. Works: prefabricated sound‑insulated units, energy retrofit (heat pump, PV on suitable roofs), shared childcare micro‑crèche at Bürkliplatz, communal kitchens, bike storage, rooftop gardens, smart building management and resident app. Partners: Stadt Zürich, gemeinnützige Wohnbaugenossenschaften, private landlords. Timeline: 6 months design & permits, 12–18 months phased retrofit.

title: Limmat Lifeline: Floating Community Clinic at Bürkliplatz for Seniors, Tourists, and Homeless
description: Convert a 20–30 m boat moored at Bürkliplatz pier (end of Bahnhofstrasse, near Bellevue) into a low‑threshold primary care and telemedicine clinic. Services: nurse triage, two GP exam rooms, vaccinations, wound care, mental‑health counseling, mobile pharmacy lockers, AEDs, preventive screenings and digital booking with language support. Target groups: Kreis 1 residents—especially seniors, shift workers, low‑income and unhoused people—and visitors. Implementation: 3 months planning with Gesundheitsdirektion and Universitätsspital Zürich, 6 months permitting, 6–9 months retrofit, 12‑month pilot with monitoring and scaling plan.

title: Rennweg–Niederdorf Hospitality & Digital Tourism Incubator for Local Workers
description: Convert vacant retail units on Rennweg and Niederdorfstrasse (near St. Peter and Helmhaus) into a public incubator with a demo kitchen, co‑working, VR/AR ‘smart tour’ lab, and pop‑up retail at Bürkliplatz. Target: 18–50 year old Kreis 1 residents, furloughed hospitality staff, migrants and youth. Partner with Zürich Tourismus, UZH Weiterbildung and local hotels on Bahnhofstrasse/Bellevue for apprenticeships. Timeline: 0–3 months planning, 4–9 renovation/equipment, 10–18 pilot training + job placements (goal: 200 trainees/year, 60 job matches).

title: Green Spine: Badenerstrasse–Bahnhof Wiedikon Pocket Parks and Rain Gardens
description: Transform Badenerstrasse (from Albisriederplatz to Bahnhof Wiedikon) into an 18‑month Green Spine: 8 pocket parks, 12 rain gardens, permeable pavements, native plantings, green walls at tram stops and a community gardening plaza at Sihlfeld. Target groups: local residents, commuters, elderly and nearby schoolchildren. Implementation: 3 months community co‑design, 12 months phased construction, 3 months commissioning. Add smart soil‑moisture sensors, monthly stewardship workshops and local volunteer planting days to ensure long‑term care and biodiversity monitoring.

title: Wiedikon Sihl Living Shoreline: Floodplain Park, Reedbeds, Boardwalk from Giesshübel to Bahnhof Wiedikon
description: Renaturalise the Sihl riverbanks between Giesshübel and Bahnhof Wiedikon into a 36‑month Living Shoreline: stepped flood terraces, floating reedbeds for biofiltration, 800m elevated boardwalk, fish passages, native meadow planting and play‑nature zones. Target groups: Wiedikon residents, schools, commuters and biodiversity. Implementation: 6 months design/permits with Canton water authorities, 18 months construction, 6 months monitoring. Integrate real‑time water‑quality and flood‑level sensors linked to Zurich warning systems and an education program for local schools and volunteer citizen science.

title: Wiedikon Mobility Hub at Bahnhof Wiedikon – EV chargers, cargo‑bike depot, last‑mile services
description: Create a 24/7 multimodal hub on the east plaza of Bahnhof Wiedikon serving residents, commuters, seniors and small businesses. Deliverables: covered secure parking for 500 bikes, 20 e‑bike/cargobike docks with maintenance bay, 10 public EV chargers, consolidated delivery lockers, and an electric neighbourhood minibus connecting Bahnhof Wiedikon → Friesenberg → Brunau (15‑minute headway). Implementation: design 6 months, construction 12 months, pilot mobility services 6 months. Partners: Stadt Zürich, VBZ, SBB, local cooperatives. Improves last‑mile logistics, reduces car trips and supports local commerce.

title: Albisriederstrasse Green Transit Corridor: protected bike lanes, smart signals, autonomous shuttle pilot
description: Transform Albisriederstrasse from Bahnhof Wiedikon to Brunaupark into a low‑traffic green transit corridor. Install 2.5 km protected bi‑directional cycle lanes, widened sidewalks, rain‑gardens at bus stops, and VBZ signal priority at Kreuzplatz and Friesenbergstrasse. Launch a 12‑month autonomous electric shuttle pilot loop serving Bahnhof Wiedikon, Friesenberg school entrances and Brunau sports complex to replace short car trips. Timeline: community planning 6 months, construction 12–18 months, shuttle pilot 12 months. Targets: schoolchildren, older residents, commuters; reduces emissions, improves safety and street life.

title: Bahnhof Wiedikon–Triemli Green Spine: Climate Corridor, Play & Community Hub for Residents
description: Transform the corridor from Bahnhof Wiedikon forecourt along Triemlistrasse to the Triemli tram terminus into a climate-resilient linear park. Install bioswales, permeable pavement, 120 native trees, solar-powered seating/chargers, sensor network (air, noise, rain), two pocket playgrounds, community garden plots, and convert an unused kiosk at Bahnhof Wiedikon into a staffed neighbourhood hub with e‑bike rental, parcel lockers and pop-up market space. Targets families, commuters, Triemli hospital staff, seniors and students. Timeline: design & participation 0–6 months, phased works 6–18 months, hub fit-out and programme 18–24 months.

title: Wiedikon Smart Clean Corridor: Sensors, Solar Bins, Community Hubs on Birmensdorferstrasse & Bahnhof Wiedikon
description: Install 20 solar-powered smart waste bins (fill/odor sensors) and 10 micro-recycling stations along Birmensdorferstrasse, Albisriederplatz and approaches to Bahnhof Wiedikon; build three staffed community cleaning hubs (micro-depots) at Bahnhof Wiedikon, Albisriederplatz and the Friesenberg tram area; pilot an autonomous sidewalk sweeper on pedestrian stretches; launch a ‘Wiedikon Clean Credit’ app to coordinate volunteers, report hotspots and reward residents/businesses. Timeline: design 3 months, procurement 4 months, install 3 months, 12‑month pilot and evaluation. Targets: residents, commuters, retailers, students.

title: Smart Safe Spine: Albisriederplatz–Bahnhof Wiedikon Corridor Safety Upgrade for Residents
description: Transform the Albisriederplatz–Bahnhof Wiedikon corridor into a Smart Safe Spine for residents, commuters, elderly and night workers. Install 25 adaptive LED lamp posts with motion/sound sensors, 6 emergency pillars linked to Schutz & Rettung/Stadtpolizei Zürich, 10 public AEDs, two raised pedestrian plazas (Albisriederplatz and Bahnhof Wiedikon), traffic-calming cushions, and 3 secure lit bike hubs. Add privacy-respecting analytics, a community safety hub in the vacant station corner, a volunteer ambassador program, and a reporting app dashboard. Timeline: 18 months (3m planning, 9m install, 6m rollout/training).

title: Wiedikon Cultural & Digital Hub at Bahnhof Wiedikon for Youth and Migrants
description: Convert upper floors above Bahnhof Wiedikon and the adjacent former Post depot at Albisriederplatz into a multilingual cultural & digital arts centre. Deliverables: five sound‑proof rehearsal rooms, 50‑seat community cinema, co‑working artist studios, VR/AR lab, podcast/recording booth, gallery, and a subsidised booking platform for local groups. Target groups: youth (12–30), migrant communities, local artists and seniors. Implementation: 6 months co‑design with residents and Theater Rigiblick, 12 months retrofit, pilot programmes months 13–18, full opening in month 19 with a year‑round calendar and digital access system.

title: Rigiblick Open‑Air Amphitheatre and Community Stage behind Theater Rigiblick
description: Build a terraced, accessible timber amphitheatre on the green slope behind Theater Rigiblick (walking 8–12 minutes from Bahnhof Wiedikon/Albisriederplatz). Features: 400 fixed and flexible seats, solar canopy, integrated sound/lighting booth, accessible ramps, storage for sets, and QR‑scannable programme signage. Programming: summer festivals, school partnerships, community residencies, intergenerational performances and refugee‑led events. Implementation: 8 months design & permits with neighborhood workshops, 10–12 months construction, soft opening in the first summer season with an annual ‘Wiedikon Culture Week’ and an open booking allotment for local groups.

title: Sihlcity–Triemli Youth STEAM & Apprenticeship Campus for Wiedikon Students
description: Convert a vacant unit in Sihlcity (near the cinema) with a satellite at Triemli Community Center (Triemlistrasse) and outdoor classrooms along Sihlfeld by Bahnhof Wiedikon. Offer 3D/CNC/robotics, VR/AR lab, bilingual coding tutors, rooftop garden on the Sihlcity parking deck, and an apprenticeship‑match program with Sihlcity retailers and local trades. Target: 10–20 year olds from Schulhaus Friesenberg, Schulhaus Wiedikon and migrant families. Timeline: 18 months (3m planning, 6m build/fit‑out, 9m pilot). Partners: Stadt Zürich Jugend, Berufsbildung Zürich, VBZ for mobility passes.

title: Albisriederplatz–Bahnhof Wiedikon Active Sports Spine: courts, pump track & learning hub
description: Reclaim lanes and plaza space along Albisriederplatz to Bahnhof Wiedikon (Manessestrasse corridor) to install two half-court basketball courts, a 3x3 court, fenced street-soccer pitch, pump track/skate elements, covered modular learning hub (storage, showers, coaches’ room) and solar LED lighting. Targets Wiedikon youth, commuters and families; integrates booking app, free after-school coaching with Schule Wiedikon and local clubs. Phased build: design & permits 6 months, construction 9–12 months, program start month 13.

title: Triemli–Uetliberg Vertical Fitness Trail with smart exercise nodes
description: Upgrade the pedestrian route from Triemli station up to Uetliberg: hardened stair sections with separated running lanes, gentler graded ramps for strollers/wheelchairs where feasible, erosion control, 12 smart exercise nodes (sensors, LED wayfinding, emergency call), rehab stations co-designed with Triemli Hospital, plus seasonal lighting and ecological planting. Targets runners, seniors, rehab patients and families and creates an annual hill-run event. Timeline: environmental approvals & design 9–12 months, construction & sensor rollout 15–24 months.

title: Wiedikon Community Hub at Bahnhof Wiedikon: Social Kitchen, Care & Co‑Working for Locals
description: Create a modular, solar‑canopied community hub on the Bahnhof Wiedikon plaza and Albisriederstrasse frontage (by the Sihl promenade): social supermarket, communal kitchen/food‑skills program, intergenerational daycare‑lounge for seniors and children (20 places), a 30‑desk low‑cost co‑working/learning lab with German‑language classes and job coaching, and a monthly neighbourhood repair café/market. Implementation: 0–6 months design & permits with Stadt Zürich and SBB, 6–12 months build (repurposed containers), 12–18 months staff training, 18–24 months pilot & launch. Targets seniors, families, migrants, unemployed youth.

title: Wiedikon Health Hub at Bahnhof Wiedikon: Integrated Care & Telemedicine for Seniors, Families, Commuters
description: Convert a vacant ground‑floor space beside Bahnhof Wiedikon (Badenerstrasse) into a 600 m² Community Health Hub offering telemedicine booths, quick biometric health kiosks, a physiotherapy gym, mental‑health group room, SPITEX satellite office and a multilingual primary‑care consultation pod. Add a mobile clinic van to run evening clinics at Brunaupark and pop‑ups at Albisriederplatz. Target groups: Friesenberg seniors, commuters, families, migrants, low‑income residents. Timeline: 3 months planning, 12 months build/outfit, 3 months staff recruitment/training, 6 months pilot. Partners: Gesundheitsdirektion Stadt Zürich, Spitex Zürich, Universitätsspital Zürich, Pro Senectute.

title: Wiedikon Jobs & Skills Hub at Bahnhof Wiedikon for Youth, Immigrants, SMEs
description: Convert underused municipal rooms and retail units adjacent to Bahnhof Wiedikon and Albisriederplatz into a 600 m² Jobs & Skills Hub: 40 hot desks, 4 maker bays (CNC, sewing, wood), digital training lab, on-site employment counselling, pop-up childcare, rooftop solar and secure bike parking by the plaza. Target groups: long‑term unemployed, youth, recent migrants, micro-entrepreneurs and local SMEs. Implementation: design 3 months, renovation 9 months, program launch month 12, three‑year pilot with Stadt Zürich Arbeitsintegration, UZH continuing education and Gewerbeverband partnerships.

title: Irchelpark Smart Orchard & Climate Hub for Oberstrass Residents and UZH
description: Transform the north meadow of Irchelpark (adjacent to Universität Zürich Irchel campus) into a community climate hub: 25 fruit and nut trees, 15 raised vegetable beds, solar-charging benches, soil‑moisture sensors and automated drip irrigation, biodiversity islands and a municipal compost station. Target groups: Oberstrass/Unterstrass residents, UZH students, local schools and seniors. Timeline: 3 months planning, 9 months planting/installation, then ongoing community workshops (monthly). Implementation by Stadtgärtnerei with a resident stewardship cooperative and free seasonal education programmes.

title: Waidberg–Bucheggplatz Green Corridor: stormwater wetlands, cycle path, biodiversity axis
description: Create a 2.5 km nature-based corridor from Waid/Waidberg (near Stadtspital Waid and Waidbad) down through Oberstrass to Bucheggplatz: daylighted bioswales and 3 constructed wetland basins (flood-retention ~10,000 m3), permeable paving, an accessible protected cycle/footpath, native tree planting, pollinator meadows, solar LED lighting and sensor-controlled overflow valves. Targets commuters, families, students, and flood resilience for Kreis 6. Timeline: design & approvals 2026, phased construction 2027–2029, with community volunteering days and an open-data sensor dashboard for water & air quality.

title: Irchel Mobility Hub: EV shuttles and cargo‑bike hub at Universität Zürich Irchel
description: Create a multimodal mobility hub at the Winterthurerstrasse/Irchelpark entrance (Universität Zürich Irchel, Kreis 6): 200 secure cargo‑ and family‑bike docks with e‑charging, sheltered repair and rental station, six on‑demand electric micro‑shuttles linking the hub to nearby tram/S‑bahn stops, real‑time displays integrated with ZVV, priority signal adjustments for shuttles, and a booking app. Targets students, staff, families and seniors. Timeline: 6 months planning + community co‑design, 6 months procurement, 12 month pilot, full operation by month 24.

title: Rigiblick–Irchelpark Green Transit Spine: protected cycleway and tram priority for Oberstrass
description: Transform the corridor connecting Kulturhaus Rigiblick to Irchelpark/Universität Zürich Irchel across Oberstrass (Kreis 6) into a 2–2.5 km green transit spine: continuous 3 m protected two‑way cycle lane, widened planted sidewalks, tram/bus priority signals at major intersections, raised pedestrian crossings, solar‑lit living bus stops with seating, and embedded air‑quality & people‑flow sensors. Includes community design workshops, school mobility programs and pop‑up car‑free festivals. Timeline: 6 months feasibility & design, 18 months phased construction to keep transit running.

title: Irchelpark Climate-Resilient Community Hub for Seniors, Students and Families (Unterstrass)
description: Convert the northwest meadow of Irchelpark beside Universität Irchel into a multifunctional community hub: rain gardens and bioswales for runoff control, a solar pergola microgrid powering lighting and an e-bike/e-cargo share, modular covered event pavilion with community kitchen and tool library, smart benches with Wi‑Fi and air-quality sensors, and intergenerational programming (senior workshops, student-led climate labs, family markets). Phases: 6‑month design and co‑creation with residents/UZH, 12‑month construction, 6‑month pilot. Targets Unterstrass/Oberstrass residents, UZH students, families, seniors.

title: Irchelpark–Rigiblick Smart Clean Corridor: sensor bins, e-bike crews for Unterstrass/Oberstrass
description: Transform the main pedestrian spine from Irchelpark Hauptweg (between Irchelstrasse and Universitätsstrasse) to Rigiblick (Rigiblickstrasse/Rigiblick theatre) with 20 solar-powered compacting sensor bins at tram stops and park entrances (Weinbergstrasse area), anti-graffiti coatings on retaining walls, five pocket-green litter traps, and four e-bike micro-cleaning teams employing local students/seniors. Add a neighbourhood reporting/reward app tied to local shops. Timeline: 0–3 months co-design with residents, 4–9 procurement/installation, 10–15 pilot & hires, 16–18 evaluate and scale.

title: Irchelpark Safe‑Night Corridor: Smart Lighting, SOS Beacons, Community Patrols for Residents
description: Pilot along main pedestrian routes inside Irchelpark and the footpaths linking Universität Irchel to Oberstrass and Unterstrass. Install 120 motion‑adaptive warm LED luminaires, 6 solar emergency SOS pillars with two‑way audio routed to Schutz & Rettung Zürich, trimmed sightlines, clear wayfinding, and a neighborhood safety app with live incident reporting. Train 24 local volunteers (students, seniors, shop owners) for scheduled accompaniment shifts. Timeline: 3 months design/permits, 9 months install, 12‑month pilot, full review and expansion plan at month 24.

title: Rigiblick Creative Campus: Convert Rigiblick Theatre & Funicular Stop into Intergenerational Arts Hub
description: Refurbish Rigiblick Theatre (Rigiblickstrasse) and the adjacent Rigiblickbahn stop into a 24‑month intergenerational arts campus: upgrade auditorium sound/lighting, add elevator and universal WC, create 4 rehearsal rooms, a livestream studio and artist co‑work space with digital booking. Target groups: Oberstrass seniors, Universität Zürich Irchel students, local artists and families. Timeline: 6 months community design and permits, 12 months construction/fit‑out, 6 months program setup. Ongoing: subsidised residencies, weekly intergenerational workshops and public performances.

title: Irchelpark Open Stage & AR Cultural Trail Linking Universität Irchel and Unterstrass Residents
description: Build a 300‑seat permanent amphitheatre at Irchelpark’s main entrance by the Universität Zürich Irchel campus and deploy a 12‑stop Augmented Reality trail telling local histories, student art and immigrant voices. Features: solar‑lit seating, multilingual audio/AR app, artist residencies, monthly open‑air festivals and school outreach. Target groups: students, families, neighbourhood schools and newcomers in Kreis 6. Timeline: 6 months design and community curation, 6 months construction and tech integration, 6 months pilot season and evaluation.

title: Irchelpark STEAM Youth Innovation Hub for Unterstrass and Oberstrass
description: Repurpose the vacant pavilion beside Sportanlage Irchel (Irchelpark, adjacent to Universität Zürich Irchel campus) into a STEAM makerspace and multilingual homework club for 6–18 year‑olds from Kreis 6. Include digital labs, woodworking/e-bike repair studio, solar roof classroom, free Wi‑Fi, loaner laptops, and a “makers‑on‑wheels” e‑trailer for school visits. Partner with UZH/ETH student mentors and local schools. Timeline: 6 months design/permits, 12 months build/fitting, pilot year with capacity ~120 youths/week and weekend community workshops.

title: Irchelpark Smart Outdoor Fitness & Community Courts for Unterstrass
description: At Irchelpark Süd, adjacent to the Universität Zürich Irchel main entrance, install a 400 m sensor-equipped fitness trail, inclusive outdoor gym stations, a 3x3 basketball court with permeable surface, two covered table-tennis bays, a 6 m bouldering wall, solar LED lighting and a booking/usage app. Target groups: students (UZH), families, seniors and clubs in Unterstrass/Oberstrass. Implementation: design + community co‑planning (3 months), phased build (9 months), training & launch programs with local sports clubs (3 months). Total 12–15 months.

title: Irchel North Multi‑Sport Dome: Year‑Round Arena, Rooftop Park, Youth Hub
description: Convert the north parking area of UZH Irchel/Irchelpark Nord into a multi‑sport dome with 4 convertible courts (basketball, futsal, volleyball), retractable roof for outdoor events, climbing wall, physiotherapy & multi-use room, secure bike garage, rooftop community park with playground and solar PV. Smart systems: real‑time occupancy, digital booking, lighting control. Partners: UZH, local schools, sports clubs. Timeline: feasibility & permits (6–9 months), build (15–18 months), operational partnerships & programs (3 months). Serves youth, students, clubs, seniors and district events.

title: Intergenerational Co‑Housing at Bucheggplatz — 60 Subsidised Units for Kreis 6 Residents
description: Convert the municipal surface lot at Bucheggplatz (Unterstrass/Oberstrass border, beside the tram stop) into a 60‑unit Wohnbaugenossenschaft building: 30% deep‑subsidy family units, 20% student micro‑units (priority to Universität Zürich/Kreis 6 students), 10 accessible senior flats. Add 15‑place on‑site childcare, community kitchen, maker space, rooftop urban garden, PV + battery + heat pump (Minergie‑P), e‑cargo bike hub and digital tenant platform. Partners: City housing office, Wohnbaugenossenschaft, UZH. Timeline: 6–12 months design & permits, 18–24 months construction, total ~3 years.

title: Unterstrass–Oberstrass Intergenerational Solidarity Hub at Weinbergstrasse
description: Convert an unused ground-floor space in the Unterstrass community centre (near Weinbergstrasse / Weinbergpark tram stop) into a resilience hub for seniors, students, families and migrants. Install a pay-what-you-can community kitchen, digital literacy lab (4 PCs, 3D-printer, Wi‑Fi), a volunteer-run repair café/maker space, rooftop allotments and 30‑person micro-shelter capacity for extreme-weather events. Timeline: months 1–3 planning & community co-design; 4–9 renovation & tech install; 10–12 pilot programmes; 13–18 scale-up, volunteer training and evaluation.

title: Irchelpark Health Hub: Preventive Care, Telemedicine & Active Aging for Unter-/Oberstrass
description: Create a community health hub in the Irchelpark pavilion (next to UZH Irchel, tram stop ‚Irchelpark‘) with a Bucheggplatz satellite (tram stop Bucheggplatz). Offer multilingual nurse-led prevention clinics, telemedicine booths linked to Stadtspital and UZH specialists, weekly mental-health drop‑ins, a 1.2 km marked fitness/walking loop with calisthenics, smart benches with SOS and air-quality sensors, a wearables loan program, and cooking-for-health classes for seniors, students and immigrant families. Timeline: 6 months planning/partnerships, 12 months fit-out, launch month 18.

title: Bucheggplatz–Milchbuck GreenTech Apprenticeship & Maker Hub for Unterstrass/Oberstrass
description: Convert a vacant municipal ground-floor near Bucheggplatz / Milchbuckstrasse into a 500 m² GreenTech hub with co‑working, three maker labs (electronics, wood, textile recycling), rooftop solar (≈30 kWp), 10 shared e‑bikes, and a digital job‑matching/AR training platform. Target groups: unemployed youth (18–30), migrants, career‑changers, and local SMEs. Partner with Stadt Zürich Wirtschaftsförderung, UZH continuing ed. and local trades. Timeline: 0–6 months planning, 6–12 months renovation & kit‑out, 12–24 months first training cohorts; 40 apprenticeship/placement targets annually.

title: Langstrasse Green Boulevard: Bioswales, Trees & Quiet Zones from Helvetiaplatz to Stauffacher
description: Transform Langstrasse (Helvetiaplatz → Stauffacher) into a low-traffic green boulevard: plant 200 native trees, install 15 bioswales and 8 pocket parks, add permeable paving, solar-lit seating and acoustic planting to reduce nightlife noise. Fit 20 air-quality and noise sensors connected to an open-data dashboard; create two nightly ‘quiet corridors’ for residents and shift-change workers. Timeline: 6 months design & permits, 18 months phased works. Targets: residents, nightlife staff, families, elderly, local businesses; managed by the city with resident co-design workshops.

title: Kreis 4 Pollinator & Green-Roof Network: 12 Roof Gardens + Tram-Stop Habitats
description: Create a biodiversity corridor across Kreis 4 by installing 12 community green roofs on cooperative housing and municipal buildings (priority sites along Langstrasse, Werdstrasse and near Helvetiaplatz), 20 pollinator shelters on tram stops (Stauffacher, Helvetiaplatz) and rainwater-harvest cisterns feeding rooftop irrigation. Include soil-moisture sensors, workshop series for schools and migrant groups, and a three-year maintenance stipend employing local residents. Timeline: year 1 surveys & training, years 2–3 installation and planting. Benefits: cooling, biodiversity, local food, jobs and climate resilience.

title: Langstrasse Safe Mobility Corridor (Helvetiaplatz–Stauffacher) for Residents
description: Create a protected two-way cycle lane and widened pedestrian zone along Langstrasse from Helvetiaplatz to Stauffacher: add 3 community cargo-bike hubs (Helvetiaplatz, Langstrasse 100, Stauffacher), curb extensions, smart LED streetlighting, real‑time air-quality sensors, and a weekend evening pedestrian plaza (cordoned 18:00–02:00). Target groups: local families, shift workers, small businesses. Timeline: 6‑month design & community co‑planning, 18‑month pilot build with evaluation and adjustment.

title: Stauffacher Multimodal Micro‑Hub with Green Overpass for Kreis 4 Commuters
description: Build a modular multimodal micro‑hub adjacent to Stauffacher tram stop with sheltered real‑time display, 200 secure bike & e‑bike charging spaces, staffed cargo‑bike workshop, lockers, and a low‑rise green pedestrian/cycle overpass linking the Stauffacher junction to the western Langstrasse neighborhoods. Integrate tram/bus priority signalling, solar canopy, and a local mobility app for bookings. Benefits commuters, elderly, parents, couriers and shops. Timeline: 9‑month detailed design, 12‑month hub construction, 18–24 months overpass delivery.

title: Langstrasse–Helvetiaplatz Community Commons: Safe, Green Hub for Kreis 4 Residents
description: Transform Langstrasse between Stauffacher and Helvetiaplatz into a weekend pedestrian commons and install a modular community hub on the Helvetiaplatz tram island. Target groups: families, migrants, youth, elderly and small businesses. Measures: removable bollards for pedestrianisation, six pocket parks replacing parking bays, solar smart streetlights, 50-space secure bike parking at Stauffacher, free Wi‑Fi, multilingual wayfinding, and a 10-container community centre (kitchen, maker space, social-worker “safe corner”, pop-up market stalls). Timeline: 24 months (6m design & consultation, 6m pilot, 12m full rollout).

title: Langstrasse & Helvetiaplatz Smart Clean Hub for Residents and Nightlife Businesses
description: Pilot a district-wide Clean Hub on the Langstrasse corridor (Langstrasse between Helvetiaplatz and Stauffacher) delivering 22:00–04:00 micro‑crews, 20 solar‑compacting smart bins with fill/odour sensors, a Helvetiaplatz community compost/drop‑off kiosk and water refill station, graffiti‑resistant street furniture, and a resident/business reporting app integrated with Stadt Zürich AWEL and VBZ. Targets: −50% visible litter in 12 months. Timeline: 3 months planning with Quartierverein Aussersihl, 6 months installation, 12‑month pilot, evaluation at 18 months. Benefits residents, night‑workers, local shops, and public transport users.

title: Langstrasse Safe Corridor: Smart Lighting, Emergency Hubs and Night Outreach for Residents & Night Workers
description: Transform Langstrasse (Helvetiaplatz → Stauffacher tram stop) with 30 warm smart-LED lamps, 6 emergency audio help pillars linked to Polizei Zürich & social services, free Wi‑Fi portals, QR maps, and three certified 'SafeHub' businesses offering refuge and first aid. Fund a 24/7 mobile outreach team (social worker + nurse + police liaison) serving residents, nightlife workers, migrants and people experiencing homelessness. Timeline: 18 months (3 months planning/community co-design, 9 months install/hiring, 6 months pilot/evaluation). Privacy-first (no CCTV) and community-governed.

title: Langstrasse Cultural Commons: Convert Warehouse into Night‑Day Arts Hub for Locals
description: Transform a vacant textile warehouse on Langstrasse (between Stauffacher tram stop and Helvetiaplatz) into a multicultural cultural commons with 3 sound‑insulated performance rooms, 10 affordable artist studios, rehearsal space, a community café, and a small licensed creche for evening events. Targets local artists, nightlife workers, immigrant communities and families. Implementation: retrofit building, install acoustic panels and ventilation, partner with Quartierverein Aussersihl and migrant arts NGOs. Timeline: design 3 months, retrofit 15 months, program launch 6 months.

title: Stauffacher–Helvetiaplatz AR Story Trail for Residents and Visitors
description: Create a bilingual (DE/EN) AR and audio story trail along Langstrasse from Stauffacher to Helvetiaplatz (including Josefstrasse and Kanzleistrasse nodes) with 25 solar‑powered info posts, QR/AR markers, community‑produced oral histories from migrant residents, youth digital workshops, and night‑safety wayfinding lighting. Targets residents, schools, tourists and night‑shift workers. Implementation: local co‑creation workshops, install posts at tram stops and parks, mobile app & web fallback, maintenance training for volunteers. Timeline: co‑creation 4 months, tech build 4 months, installation 4 months, pilot 3 months.

title: Langstrasse STEAM & Social Hub at Helvetiaplatz for 12–25-Year-Olds
description: Convert a vacant ground-floor space at Helvetiaplatz (next to the weekly market) into a youth-run STEAM & social hub serving 12–25‑year-olds from Kreis 4. Facilities: makerspace (3D printers, CNC, laser, recording booth), free high-speed Wi‑Fi, language café, green rooftop garden, counselling rooms. Program: coding & trades bootcamps, AR local-history trail on Langstrasse, apprenticeship matchmaking app co-run with local businesses near Hardbrücke and Viadukt. Timeline: 3-month co-design with a youth council, 9-month renovation, 12-month pilot, ongoing governance by youth-panel and Sozialdepartement partners.

title: Covered Langstrassenpark Multi‑Sport Pavilion and Community Hub (near Volkshaus)
description: Build a heated, all‑weather pavilion on the south edge of Langstrassenpark (adjacent to Volkshaus/Stauffacher) with a 30x18m convertible court (basketball, futsal, handball), indoor skate/parkour zone, 6m climbing wall, LED smart lighting, and a privacy‑respecting booking app. Target groups: youth, migrant families, seniors, Primarschule Aussersihl. Implementation: 0–3 months design & community workshops at Volkshaus, 3–9 months permits with Stadt Zürich (Tiefbauamt, Sportamt), 9–24 months construction, 24+ months programme rollout with local clubs.

title: Stauffacher Parkour & Street‑Sports Plaza with Night Leagues (Stauffacherstrasse)
description: Transform the empty strip beside Tram stop Stauffacher/Stauffacherstrasse into a modular street‑sports plaza with skate‑friendly surfaces, adjustable parkour obstacles, two 3x3 basketball half‑courts, ping‑pong tables, ambient LED safety lighting, and low‑noise surfacing. Add a community coaching programme, gender‑balanced night leagues, and a sensor‑controlled lighting and booking system. Target groups: teenagers, young adults, women, neighbourhood sports groups. Timeline: 0–4 months co‑design with Jugendtreffs and Polizei, 4–12 months build and pilot leagues, ongoing maintenance by Kreis‑4 sports partners.

title: Helvetiaplatz Modular Co‑Housing: 70 Affordable Units + Community Hub for Langstrasse
description: Convert the municipal surface parking at Helvetiaplatz (Langstrasse quarter, near Stauffacher tram stop) into a 4‑storey prefabricated building with 70 energy‑efficient units (40 studios, 20 one‑beds, 10 two‑beds). Target groups: low‑income families, young professionals, refugees and local artists. Ground floor: community kitchen, 10‑place childcare, co‑working and neighbourhood services; roof: 500 m² urban garden + PV. 200 secure bike spaces and EV chargers. Delivery: 6 months participatory design, 12 months permits/prefab, 12 months on‑site assembly (30 months total). 20% deep‑subsidy social housing, smart energy management.

title: Helvetiaplatz 24/7 Community Hub & Night Support Centre for Langstrasse Residents and Night Workers
description: Convert the ground-floor municipal space at Helvetiaplatz (corner Langstrasse / Stauffacher) into a 24/7 low‑threshold Community Hub: 30 modular micro‑shelter beds, pay‑what‑you‑can community kitchen, multilingual legal/health drop‑in, evening outreach van, and co‑working/training rooms for local entrepreneurs and youth. Redesign the plaza with solar canopy, sensor-based safety lighting (no intrusive cameras), and a service app for bookings. Partners: Stadt Zürich Soziale Dienste, HEKS/Caritas, local NGOs. Timeline: 18 months planning/renovation + 3‑year pilot with quarterly evaluations and replication plan for other Kreise.

title: Langstrasse–Helvetiaplatz Integrated Health Hub: Mobile Clinic, Mental Care, Harm Reduction
description: Create a modular Health Hub anchored at Helvetiaplatz with a parked mobile clinic, weekly pop-up kiosks along Langstrasse (near Kanzleistraße intersection) and outreach at Stauffacher tram stop. Services: primary care, low-threshold mental-health counselling, wound care, vaccinations, naloxone distribution, harm-reduction advice, multilingual telehealth booths and a rooftop community therapy garden. Target groups: residents, migrants, sex workers, people experiencing homelessness and elderly. Implementation: 0–3 months planning with Stadt Zürich/Gesundheitsdirektion and Suchthilfe partners; 4–9 months retrofit/permits; 10–18 months pilot with KPIs (ER visits, vaccinations, counselling sessions, overdose reversals).

title: Langstrasse Skills & Night-Economy Hub: Training, Microbusinesses, and Job-Matching for Aussersihl Residents
description: Convert vacant ground-floor shops along Langstrasse (between Stauffacher and Helvetiaplatz) into a 24-month Langstrasse Skills & Night‑Economy Hub: coworking (20 pods), commercial training kitchen, makerlab, evening hospitality training, and micro-retail pop-up stage. Target: unemployed youth, migrants, hospitality/night-shift workers, and local micro-entrepreneurs. Install multilingual digital job-kiosks at Stauffacher and Helvetiaplatz and an integrated job-matching platform linked to Stadt Zürich Jobcenter. Timeline: 0–6m planning/partnerships (ZHdK, Caritas Zürich, local Gewerbe), 6–12m retrofit & pilot, 12–24m scale with monthly Langstrasse Night Market pop-ups.

title: Wipkingen Limmat Green Corridor: Flood-Safe Riverside for Residents and Students
description: Transform the Limmat stretch from Bahnhof Wipkingen to Wipkingerbrücke into a multi-level green corridor: terraced bioswales, native willows and alder belts, floodable pocket parks, permeable paving, solar LED wayfinding, a raised wooden boardwalk for pedestrians/cargo e-bikes, and realtime water-level sensors linked to a neighbourhood alert app. Partner with Schulhaus Wipkingen for outdoor classrooms and community planting days. Phased delivery over 24 months, benefits commuters, families, seniors, and climate resilience for Kreis 10.

title: Höngg Solar Rain-Roof Network: Retrofit Public Roofs for Energy, Water, Cooling
description: Create a district-wide retrofit on public roofs around Hönggerplatz and Hönggerstrasse (Schulhaus Höngg, Gemeindehaus, Hallenbad Höngg, community centres): modular PV arrays, extensive green roofs, rooftop cisterns for irrigation/fire reserve, and smart sensors feeding an open dashboard. Results: local renewable energy, lower summer heat, stormwater retention, vocational training for apprentices, and targeted energy credits for low-income households. Implementation with EWZ and city building services in a 36-month programme with pilot on two roofs in year one.

title: Hönggerberg Funicular & E‑Shuttle Link: Barrier‑Free Connection to Wipkingen S‑Bahn
description: Install a small funicular (incline tram) from ETH Hönggerberg / Science City (upper Hönggerberg) down to Wipkingen S‑Bahn station with an intermediate stop near Waidspital/Hönggerplatz. Features: wheelchair and cargo‑bike capable cars, integrated ZVV fares, real‑time displays, and electric feeder shuttles for steep side streets. Targets students, commuters, elderly and families; reduces steep bus routing and private car trips. Implementation: feasibility study 6–12 months, planning 12–18 months, construction 24–30 months. Partners: Stadt Zürich Verkehr, ETH, VBZ, SBB.

title: Kreis 10 Smart Mobility Corridor: Protected Bike Highway, Cargo‑Hubs & Bus Priority
description: Create a continuous protected bike/roll corridor from Wipkingenbrücke through Wipkingen Bahnhof → Hönggerstrasse → Hönggerplatz to the Waid area, plus three Mobility Hubs (Wipkingen Bahnhof, Hönggerplatz, ETH Hönggerberg) with 200 secure bike spaces, e‑cargo bike fleet, e‑bike charging and parcel consolidation lockers. Add smart traffic signals with dynamic bus priority at Tram/Bus junctions to cut delays. Targets commuters, families, local shops and delivery logistics. Timeline: pilot lane & two hubs within 12–18 months, full corridor + signal upgrades 24–30 months. Partners: VBZ, Tiefbauamt, local co‑ops.

title: Wipkingen Bahnhofplatz Limmat Resilience Hub — green plaza, community services for Kreis 10 residents
description: Convert Wipkingen Bahnhofplatz and the adjacent Limmat riverside (Wipkingerbrücke → riverbank stretch north of the station) into a flood‑resilient green plaza and modular community hub. Deliverables: raised bioswale terraces, pocket community gardens, solar canopy with e‑bike/e‑cargo charging, modular container hub with childcare room, evening co‑working & maker space, public WC, and air‑quality/noise sensors. Targets: families, elderly, commuters, ETH Hönggerberg students, local shops. Timeline: design & permits 6 months (2025 Q3–Q4), pilot pop‑up 2026 Q1, phased construction 2026–2027, full operation 2028.

title: Wipkingen–Höngg Smart Clean Corridor: Sensors, Robot Sweepers, Community Hubs for Residents
description: Pilot a clean-streets corridor linking Wipkingen SBB, Wipkingenbrücke/Wipkingerplatz, Höngg Bahnhof and Katzensee access points: install 12 solar compacting smart bins with fill/GPS sensors, 3 electric pedestrian-zone sweep robots, two community clean-hubs with bulky-waste repair café and tool library, and a multilingual neighbourhood ambassador program. Integrate sensor data with the city's reporting platform and run education pop-ups at Hönggerberg/ETH student gates. Timeline: 6 months planning, 12-month pilot, evaluation & scale-up. Targets commuters, families, students, elderly and local businesses.

title: Wipkingen–Hönggerstrasse Smart Safety Corridor and Community Hub for Residents
description: Create a connected safety corridor from Bahnhof Wipkingen along Wipkingerbrücke to Hönggerstrasse with 12 adaptive LED streetlights, 6 solar emergency call pillars, 4 privacy-first CCTV nodes, and a staffed Community Safety Hub in the unused kiosk at Bahnhof Wipkingen. Targets commuters, elderly residents, shift workers and schoolchildren. Includes a neighbourhood safety app, volunteer steward training, multilingual signage, and monthly safety workshops. Phases: 3‑month planning, 9‑month pilot (lighting, 2 calls, hub), 6‑month full roll‑out. Operates with Stadt Zürich Polizei coordination and strict data/privacy rules.

title: Wipkingen–Höngg Cultural Corridor: Limmat Stage, Viaduct Studios, AR Walk for Residents
description: Create a continuous cultural corridor linking Bahnhof Wipkingen, Wipkingerplatz, under the Wipkingen viaduct and Hönggerstrasse to ETH Hönggerberg. Install a moored floating stage on the Limmat by Bahnhof Wipkingen, convert three viaduct bays into soundproof rehearsal/atelier studios, deploy AR interpretive plaques and a booking app for pop-up performances. Target: local artists, families, youth, migrants, seniors. Timeline: 30 months (6m design & permits, 18m construction/fit-out, 6m program launch). Includes solar lighting, accessible ramps, multilingual programming and community curation panels.

title: Höngg Intergenerational Digital Story Lab at Reformierte Kirche and Schulhaus Höngg for Residents
description: Turn space in Reformierte Kirche Höngg and the local Schulhaus Höngg into a digital oral-history & media lab with recording booths, translation services, workshops for seniors, schoolchildren, and migrant groups. Produce a public digital archive hosted with Stadtbibliothek Zürich, guided storytelling walks along Hönggerstrasse and Wipkingenstrasse, and AR plaques at community sites. Specific improvements: podcast studio, editing suite, outreach coordinator, volunteer training. Timeline: 18 months (6m setup & training, 6m pilot with schools, 6m public rollout).

title: Hönggerberg–Wipkingen Youth Innovation Campus: STEAM Labs, Apprenticeships, Community Makerspace
description: Create a district-scale youth campus linking ETH Hönggerberg outreach rooms (after school STEAM labs), a mobile makerspace parked weekly at Wipkingen SBB forecourt, and a Hönggerstrasse ‘green skills’ training rooftop on the outreach building. Target 10–25 year-olds from Höngg and Wipkingen, local Primarschulen and apprentices. Implementation: 0–6 months planning with ETH and schools; 6–12 months refurb (two lab rooms, tool safety, solar demo roof); 12–24 months pilot open weekdays 15–19h, weekend workshops and quarterly apprenticeship fairs. Focus: hands-on tech, green skills, mentorship and local employer placement.

title: Hönggerberg Community Sports & Innovation Campus — multi‑age hub at Hönggerberg
description: Transform vacant municipal plot adjacent to ETH Hönggerberg (near Hönggerstrasse 82) into a 3‑floor sports & innovation campus with indoor athletics hall, climbing wall, flexible courts, youth fitness studio, senior-friendly movement room, rooftop solar and heat‑pump heating. Target groups: school classes, FC Höngg youth, seniors, refugees. Implementation: design 6–9 months, build 24 months, community co‑programming launched month 30. Smart features: booking app, occupancy sensors, integrated sports‑science pilot programs run with ETH Hönggerberg.

title: Wipkingen Limmat Active Corridor — riverside trail, courts and year‑round water access
description: Build a resilient active corridor along the Limmat from Wipkingen Bahnhof to Höngg Dorfplatz: 1.2 km paved fitness trail, three calisthenics nodes, flood‑resistant half basketball court, pumptrack, inclusive outdoor gym, safe kayak/canoe launch and changing container. Target groups: families, commuters, immigrant women’s groups, youth. Implementation: phased works (planning 4 months, river engineering & path 10 months, facilities 4 months), community programming and seasonal sport festivals from month 12. Smart elements: motion LED lighting, free Wi‑Fi hotspot, QR exercise tutorials in DE/EN/AR/FR.

title: Hönggerstrasse Modular Co‑Housing & Senior Hub between Hönggerplatz and Wipkingen S‑Bahn for Families & Elderly
description: Convert vacant municipal plots and underused ground floors along Hönggerstrasse (between Hönggerplatz and Wipkingen S‑Bahn) into a 48‑unit timber modular, energy‑positive co‑housing cooperative. Mix 1–4‑room apartments with 30% set as below‑market social rents, an intergenerational day‑hub (15 childcare places), shared kitchen, makerspace and digital resident platform. Add green roofs, PV, rainwater reuse and a mobility hub with 10 e‑bike chargers beside Wipkingen station. Implementation: cooperative + city lease, 9 months design/permits, 27 months build, completed within 36 months.

title: Höngg–Wipkingen Community Health & Active Aging Hub at Bahnhof Wipkingen
description: Transform an unused municipal building beside Bahnhof Wipkingen into a Höngg–Wipkingen Health & Active Living Hub with primary care, physiotherapy, mental-health rooms, community rehab gym and subsidised community kitchen. Install three solar-powered telemedicine kiosks (Bahnhof Wipkingen, Limmat riverside in Wipkingen, ETH Hönggerberg) and a sensor-enabled Limmat walking loop for fall detection and activity tracking. Target groups: older residents, commuters, ETH students, families. Timeline: Phase 1 (0–12 months) pilot kiosks and partnerships with Gesundheitsamt ZH and ETH; Phase 2 (12–30 months) retrofit and open hub; Phase 3 (30–48 months) expand and evaluate.

title: Wipkingen–Höngg Innovation Hub at Wipkingen Bahnhof for Local Startups and Apprentices
description: Convert the vacant municipal pavilion at Wipkingen Bahnhofplatz and street-level space on Hönggerstrasse into a 650 m² Innovation Hub: 50 subsidised coworking desks, wood/metal makerlab, digital skills lab (3D printers, VR), solar canopy and childcare corner. Target groups: unemployed youth, migrants, parents returning to work, local microentrepreneurs. Partners: ETH Hönggerberg, Gewerbeverein Höngg‑Wipkingen. Timeline: 3 months design, 12 months renovation/equipment, 12‑month pilot. Deliverables: bilingual trainings, an online job‑matching portal, quarterly job fairs at the hub and 150 trainees/50 new microbusinesses within 24 months.

title: Create Limmat Floating Wetlands (Technopark–Schiffbau) for Kreis 5 Residents
description: Three‑year project to install a 300–500 m chain of modular floating wetland platforms on the Limmat between Technopark/Escher‑Wyss‑Platz and Schiffbau. Targets residents, commuters and aquatic biodiversity: reedbeds, native plants, fish shelters, solar LED safety lights and electric boat charging. Add IoT water‑quality sensors and an open dashboard; community steward program with local schools and volunteer planting days. Year 1 permits/design; Year 2 construction; Year 3 monitoring, adaptive management and education programming.

title: Langstrasse–Escher‑Wyss Green Spine: Climate‑Resilient Street Retrofit for Residents & Businesses
description: Ambitious 4‑year corridor upgrade along Langstrasse, Geroldstrasse, Pfingstweidstrasse and Escher‑Wyss‑Platz: permeable pavements, 120 mature street trees, bioswales, green façades on selected buildings (Langstrasse 120–140), an underground cistern at Escher‑Wyss‑Platz to harvest roof/runoff for irrigation, solar pergolas with e‑bike charging at Hardbrücke and Viadukt, and 10 community micro‑farm plots in the Viadukt/Geroldareal. Phase 1 pilot on Langstrasse (year 1); full roll‑out years 2–4 with smart irrigation sensors and local jobs training.

title: Escher‑Wyss/Hardbrücke Mobility Hub: Secure Bike Parking, Cargo Bikes & Parcel Hub
description: Create a multimodal hub between Escher‑Wyss‑Platz and Hardbrücke (Pfingstweidstrasse 10–30) serving residents, commuters, SMEs and couriers. Install 1,200 covered secure bicycle spaces, 100 e‑cargo bikes for short‑term rental, 50 parcel lockers, four digital mobility kiosks with ZVV realtime displays and ticketing, and dedicated last‑mile loading bays in the Viadukt arches. Implementation: design 6 months, tender 6 months, build 12 months, pilot operations 12 months. Integrate an app for availability, partner with SBB, VBZ and local logistics firms; priority for local residents' subscriptions.

title: Schiffbaustrasse Green Tram Boulevard: Rapid Trams, Protected Cycleways, Pocket Plazas
description: Transform Schiffbaustrasse from Escher‑Wyss‑Platz through Schiffbau to Hardbrücke into a tram‑prioritised boulevard: a continuous 2‑lane tram corridor with sensor‑driven priority, 3.0m physically separated cycle lanes each side, widened pavements, six pocket plazas (near Schiffbau, Technopark and Viadukt), stormwater bio‑swales and LED lighting. Target groups: local families, commuters, students and cultural visitors. Implementation: feasibility & community engagement 9 months, phased construction 24 months (night/weekend works to preserve traffic), full opening 36 months. Remove through car lanes, relocate parking to smart garages at Pfingstweidstrasse.

title: Pfingstweid Linear Green Commons: Resilient Park & Community Hubs for Kreis 5 (Hardbrücke–Escher-Wyss)
