description: Transform Pfingstweidstrasse corridor from Hardbrücke to Escher-Wyss-Platz into a 700m linear green commons: raised bioswale park, shaded solar-canopy cycle lane, floodable plaza near Schiffbau, 3 community hubs (at Technopark stop, Viadukt/Frau Gerold’s Garten, Escher-Wyss tram), inclusive playground, rooftop community gardens, and biodiversity pockets. Target groups: families, seniors, students, Technopark workers, local businesses. Add IoT soil/air sensors, dynamic LED safety lighting, and a booking app for hubs. Timeline: design & co‑creation 2025–2026, phased construction 2026–2028, programming from 2027.

title: Smart Clean Corridor Escher-Wyss–Hardbrücke: Sensors, EV Sweepers, Community Hub
description: Deploy a 12–24 month pilot to transform Pfingstweidstrasse, Escher-Wyss-Platz, Viadukt arches (Im Viadukt) and the Schiffbaustrasse riverside: install 40 solar compacting sensor bins, 2 electric street sweepers, 1 graffiti-removal trailer, and a staffed mobile cleaning hub under the Viadukt. Hire 8 local residents as a social-enterprise crew, run a citizen reporting app and real-time cleanliness map, and partner with VBZ and local businesses. Timeline: 6 months planning, 12 month pilot, scale in year 2.

title: Hardplatz–Viadukt NightSafe Hub: 24/7 Staffed Safety, Lighting, SOS Pillars for Kreis 5 Residents
description: Create two staffed Safe Corners (converted containers) at Hardplatz (Hohlstrasse/Hardbrücke) and Viadukt/Schiffbau, operate 22:00–04:00; install 10 smart adaptive LED streetlights along Pfingstweidstrasse and Viadukt, 6 emergency SOS pillars linked to Stadtpolizei at Hardbrücke, Toni-Areal tram stop and Geroldstrasse market, and 12 secure bike lockers at Hardbrücke. Use privacy-preserving motion sensors (no facial recognition) feeding a community dashboard at the hub. Train 30 local Night Ambassadors for outreach, de-escalation and first aid. Timeline: 6 months planning, 12 months construction and pilot (18 months total).

title: Im Viadukt: Affordable Artist Studios, Makerspaces and Community Gallery for Kreis 5
description: Convert three Viadukt arches beside the Viaduktstrasse/Hardbrücke into 20 subsidised studios, a shared wood/metal/electronics makerspace, public gallery and bilingual outreach office. Target groups: local visual artists, youth, migrant creatives and cultural startups. Improvements: soundproofing, accessible entrances, solar lighting, digital booking platform, monthly open-studio nights. Implementation: 6 months planning with community co-design, 12 months retrofit, public launch at 18 months. Managed by a non-profit with tiered rents and residency bursaries.

title: Sihlquai/Schiffbau Cultural Pier: Floating Stage, Artists' Micro‑Housing and Year‑Round Festivals
description: Build a mixed-use cultural pier at Schiffbau plaza (Sihlquai) with a modular floating stage, terraced seating, dock for community boats, and 12 micro-apartments for artists above the pier. Target groups: families, schools, touring musicians, refugee and low-income residents. Features: modular festival infrastructure, solar canopy, stormwater planters, AR-guided district cultural trail linking Escher-Wyss-Platz and Hardbrücke, community-curated summer season and winter indoor programme. Timeline: 12-month pilot floating stage, full construction 24–36 months, annual festival calendar thereafter.

title: Viadukt Youth Tech & Green Makers Hub at Hardbrücke for Kreis 5 Teens
description: Transform vacant Viadukt arches near Viaduktstrasse (opposite Frau Gerold's Garten, ~250m from Hardbrücke S‑Bahn) into a youth makerspace and urban learning centre for ages 10–25 (priority: multilingual immigrant youth and school dropouts). Install 3D printers, CNC bench, electronics lab, VR studio, classroom for German/tutoring, rooftop urban garden for food-tech lessons, secure bike parking and free Wi‑Fi. Partner with Technopark Zürich, Prime Tower companies and Theater Schiffbau for mentorship and internships. Timeline: design & permits 6 months, fit‑out 9–12 months, 18‑month pilot; target 1,000 participants/year and 150 internships.

title: Pfingstweid Smart Sports Park: Bouldering, Calisthenics, Lighted Court (Pfingstweidpark)
description: Transform the Pfingstweidpark strip beside Technopark Zurich (Pfingstweidstrasse, near Bahnhof Hardbrücke) into a year-round smart sports park: 12–20m modular bouldering and adaptive climbing walls, accessible calisthenics lines, a 15×28m hybrid-multiuse court with solar LED floodlighting, IoT sensors for usage analytics and safety, an app for bookings/community coaching, and weekly coached sessions for schools, shift workers, seniors and refugees. Implementation: 3 months design & permits, 9 months construction, 6 months program rollout with local clubs and youth services.

title: Hardbrücke Micro‑Stadium & Active Hub at Hardturmstrasse for Clubs and Schools
description: Convert the Hardturm/Hardbrücke site (between Hardturmstrasse, Sihlquai and Pfingstweidstrasse, across from Prime Tower and Schiffbau) into a modular 1,200–1,500 seat micro‑stadium with retractable stands, rooftop 200m running loop, indoor hall for futsal/basketball/climbing, VR training lab, community sport incubator and green terraces. Features: solar canopy, flood-proof event plaza, integrated booking/booking-prioritisation for Kreis 5 schools, youth clubs and NGOs, evening hours for shift workers. Implementation: 6 months participatory design with local clubs, 18–24 months phased construction, phased opening for community programs.

title: Viadukt–Pfingstweid Modular Mixed‑Income Housing and Community Hub for Kreis 5
description: Convert vacant Viadukt arches and adjacent plots along Pfingstweidstrasse (between Hardbrücke and Escher‑Wyss‑Platz, next to Toni‑Areal) into 120 modular apartments: 40 subsidised, 20 social housing, 60 market/co‑living units. Add ground‑floor community kitchen, childcare (8 places), neighbourhood coworking, social services office, rooftop PV, battery, green roofs and play gardens linking to Hardturmpark. Target: low‑income families, seniors, young professionals, refugees. Implementation: 6 months design + community co‑creation, 9 months permits, 18 months prefabricated construction (total ≈33 months) in partnership with Wohnbaugenossenschaften and Stadt Zürich.

title: Toni-Areal Community Commons: Makerspace, Childcare & Digital Lab for Kreis 5
description: Convert 800 m² ground-floor at Pfingstweidstrasse 96 (adjacent Pfingstweidpark, 5 min from Hardbrücke) into an intergenerational hub. Target groups: Hardturm/Hardau families, seniors, ZHdK students, artists, refugees. Includes 200 m² makerspace, 100 m² digital inclusion lab, 100 m² childcare (8–12 places), 150 m² cooperative low-cost grocery, weekly legal/social clinic, rooftop garden with solar (≈30 kWp) and beehives, secure bike hub and 2 EV chargers. Smart features: booking app, occupancy sensors, free Wi‑Fi, digital learning kiosks. Timeline: planning 6 months, renovation 9 months, 12‑month pilot programs.

title: Toni-Areal Pfingstweid Health Hub: Integrated Primary Care, Telemedicine & Community Therapy for Kreis 5
description: Convert Toni-Areal ground floor (Pfingstweidstrasse 96) into a public Pfingstweid Health Hub: walk‑in primary care, low‑threshold mental health & addiction drop‑in, bilingual telemedicine booths, and rooftop therapeutic garden. Deploy a mobile clinic van serving Escher‑Wyss‑Platz, Hardbrücke S‑bahnhof and the Geroldstrasse market. Include digital scheduling, air‑quality sensors and a community health data lab in partnership with UZH/ETH. Targets residents, commuters, elderly, migrants and people with substance‑use needs. Timeline: planning 0–6 months, renovation & tech 6–18 months, pilot 18–30 months, full operation by month 36.

title: Viadukt Social Fabrication Hub at Pfingstweid — Job Training & Micro‑enterprises for Kreis 5 Residents
description: Transform Viadukt arches and a vacant hall on Pfingstweidstrasse (between Hardbrücke and Escher-Wyss-Platz) into a 'Social Fabrication Hub' offering maker labs (CNC, 3D printing, textiles), subsidized micro‑workspaces, business coaching, and a social procurement corridor linking Viadukt retailers, restaurants, and Zurich West firms. Target: unemployed residents, migrants, youth (16–30), and small entrepreneurs. Timeline: 0–6 months planning with Stadt Zürich, ZHAW/ETH and Viadukt tenants; 6–18 months retrofit (solar, ventilation, safety); 18–36 months pilot. Goal: train 200 people, seed 100 microenterprises, create 120 jobs in 3 years.

title: Oerlikon Green Corridor: Bioswales, Urban Forest & Smart Air Monitoring (Bahnhof Oerlikon→Hallenstadion)
description: Create a 1.6 km green corridor along the axis from Bahnhof Oerlikon plaza via Messeplatz to Hallenstadion: install linear bioswales on Wallisellenstrasse frontage, plant 500 native trees and pollinator meadows, add permeable pavements and solar LED seating, and deploy 12 real-time air/noise sensors feeding Zürich open data. Benefits commuters, nearby residents (Oerlikon, Seefeld), schoolchildren and Hallenstadion visitors. Implementation: 6 months design & stakeholder engagement, 18 months phased construction, maintenance plan with local associations from month 25.

title: Katzensee Gateway: Climate-Resilient Wetland, Community Bathing and Learning Hub (Seebach/Affoltern)
description: Restore and expand the Katzensee wetland fringe to improve biodiversity, water quality and flood buffering; add a natural swimming platform, accessible boardwalk from Seebach Bahnhof (via Seebacherstrasse path), reed-bed filtration and a low-energy learning hub with classrooms and citizen science lab. Targets: families, Primarschulen in Seebach/Affoltern, seniors and migrant groups. Timeline: 6 months ecological survey/community co-design, 18 months restoration and boardwalk, 12 months hub build (overlap), with volunteer stewardship and school curricula integration.

title: Oerlikon Multimodal Hub: Secure Bike, Cargo-Bike Depot & Real-Time Info at Bahnhof Oerlikon
description: Create a flagship mobility hub on Bahnhofplatz Oerlikon / Hohenbühlstrasse: 300 secure long-term bike spaces, 30 shared e-cargo bikes (library model) for deliveries/parents/local shops, 50 short-term sheltered e-bike/scooter docks, 4 EV chargers, parcel consolidation room for Messe Zürich/Hallenstadion, and ZVV-integrated real-time displays. Targets commuters, event visitors, SMEs and seniors. Implementation: design + permit 6 months, construction 9–12 months, launch 12–18 months with community workshops and monthly usage monitoring.

title: Hallenstadion–Messe Low-Emission Event Mobility Zone with e-Shuttles from Seebach & Affoltern
description: Pilot a low-emission event zone around Hallenstadion, Messe Zürich and Bahnhof Oerlikon: temporary pedestrianisation of the immediate forecourt on Wallisellenstrasse during major events, a consolidated goods & loading hub on Hohenbühlstrasse, and two demand-responsive electric shuttle lines (Seebach ⇄ Oerlikon ⇄ Affoltern centre) with bus-priority signals on Schaffhauserstrasse. Includes booking app, real-time displays at Bahnhof Seebach and Bahnhof Oerlikon, outreach to local residents and a 12-month trial with traffic, noise and air-quality evaluation.

title: Smart Clean Corridor Oerlikon: Sensor Bins, Community Teams for Messe/Hallenstadion Visitors
description: Install 25 solar compacting sensor bins and 6 micro-stations (waste-sorting + bike pump) at Bahnhof Oerlikon forecourt, Hallenstadion/Messe plazas, MFO-Park, Seebach Bahnhof area and Katzensee access points. Form a trained 'Clean Crew' of local residents and youth for post-event sweeps, graffiti-to-mural conversions and targeted street-surface cleansing to reduce stormwater pollution. Integrate an IoT dashboard with VBZ/SBB for optimized collection routes and a gamified app rewarding volunteers with local vouchers. Timeline: 18-month pilot (3m planning, 6m install/training, 9m operation & evaluation).

title: Oerlikon–Seebach Night Safety Network: Solar Plazas, Call Pillars, Ambassadors
description: Install six solar LED micro-plazas and eight emergency call pillars at Bahnhof Oerlikon forecourt, Hallenstadion plaza, MFO-Park entrances, Seebach Bahnhofplatz and Bremgartenstrasse. Recruit and train 12 Night Ambassadors (local hires/volunteers) for de-escalation, first aid, and multilingual assistance; integrate a bilingual emergency-app link to Stadtpolizei and Zurich social services; add smart-motion lighting on key pedestrian/cycle corridors. Timeline: 6 months community planning, 9 months installation and training, 3 months pilot & evaluation. Targets commuters, concertgoers, youth and elderly; privacy-compliant, no permanent CCTV.

title: Hallenstadion–Oerlikon Cultural Incubator: Studios, Black Box, Outdoor Stage for Kreis 11 Artists
description: Create a year‑round cultural hub adjacent to Hallenstadion and Bahnhof Zürich Oerlikon (Oerlikerplatz/Wallisellenstrasse). Retrofit two underused commercial units beneath Oerlikon station into soundproof rehearsal studios, a digital production lab and artist residencies; build a 200‑seat flexible black‑box theatre in the Hallenstadion annex and a modular outdoor stage in Oerlikerpark. Target groups: local musicians, theatre ensembles, youth and migrant creatives. Implementation: planning 6 months, retrofit and build 18 months, community programming immediately thereafter with subsidised rehearsal slots and seasonal festivals.

title: Kreis 11 Living History AR Trail: Seebach–Oerlikon–Affoltern Story Route for Schools & Neighbours
description: Design a bilingual (DE/EN) augmented‑reality cultural trail linking Bahnhof Seebach, Seebacherplatz, the Schaffhauserstrasse corridor, Oerlikerpark and Affoltern Zentrum (Kirche Affoltern). Commission 30 site‑specific murals, audio stories and AR scenes co‑created with local elders, migrant groups and Schulhaus classes. Install durable QR nodes, benches and interpretive signage; deliver an app with multilingual narration (also ALB/PRT/SRB). Timeline: 6‑month pilot (10 nodes) then full rollout at 18 months; annual Story Festival and school curriculum integration for lasting community stewardship.

title: Oerlikon–Seebach Youth Innovation Hub: STEM Lab, Vocational Training, Mobile FabLab
description: Convert vacant city-owned ground-floor space at Bahnhof Oerlikon (west plaza, adjacent to Hallenstadion/Messe Zürich) into an after-school STEM & vocational makerspace (10 workstations, 3D printers, CNC, VR lab, language support). Add a mobile FabLab van serving Seebach Bahnhof and Affoltern Zentrum for pop-up workshops. Target 10–25-year-olds (school students, apprentices, migrant youth). Partner with Messe Zürich exhibitors, local trades and Berufsbildungszentren for internships. Implementation: 6 months planning, 12 months conversion + equipment, 12-month pilot with monthly hackathons and quarterly evaluation.

title: Hallenstadionplatz Community Sports Campus — Inclusive hub next to Bahnhof Oerlikon
description: Convert the Hallenstadionplatz surface parking (adjacent to Hallenstadion / Messe Zürich, Bahnhof Oerlikon) into a year‑round community sports campus with 2 indoor multiuse courts, a concussion‑safe indoor skate/bouldering hall, accessible hydrotherapy pool, coaching rooms and club storage. Target groups: youth (10–25), seniors, people with disabilities, local clubs and schools. Implementation: design & build 30 months, solar canopy, digital booking app, partnership with Sportamt Zürich and local Vereine, community programming and subsidised slots for low‑income residents.

title: Kreis 11 Active Spine: 4km day/night running & bike loop linking Seebach–Oerlikon–Affoltern
description: Create a protected 4 km Active Spine along Schaffhauserstrasse → Hofwiesenstrasse → Seebacherstrasse connecting Bahnhof Seebach, Bahnhof Oerlikon and Affoltern Zentrum. Install separated running/cycling lanes, seven smart exercise nodes (calisthenics, table tennis, mini courts), solar LED night lighting with motion sensors, real‑time counters and an app for bookings, events and leagues. Timeline: phased 18–24 months. Benefits: safe active commuting, inclusive sports access for all ages, district leagues and health programmes in partnership with schools and youth centres.

title: Seebach Depot Airspace: 120 Affordable Modular Homes, Daycare and Senior Hub for Kreis 11 Residents
description: Build 120 modular mixed-size apartments above the city-owned operations site near Bahnhof Seebach / Seebacherplatz. Target groups: young families, seniors downsizing, students, refugees and essential workers. Include 20% permanently below-market units, ground-floor community centre with 40-place childcare, intergenerational common rooms, rooftop communal gardens, 200 bike spots, PV, heat-pump systems and smart tenant app. Resident cooperative governance ensures local allocation. Timeline: feasibility & co-design 0–12 months, planning/permitting 12–24, modular construction 24–42 months, phased occupancy by month 42–48.

title: Oerlikon–Seebach Community Resilience Hubs for Families, Seniors and Migrants
description: Convert vacant municipal ground-floor spaces at Oerlikerplatz (by Oerlikon Bahnhof) and a wing near Seebacherplatz into three Community Resilience Hubs offering multilingual social counselling, subsidised drop-in childcare, intergenerational day space, digital-literacy lab with public Wi‑Fi, maker space and community kitchen. Add a mobile outreach van serving Affolternstrasse stops and Seebach Bahnhof, solar panels, and a smart booking/translation app. Partners: Stadt Zürich Sozialdepartement and local NGOs. Timeline: 6‑month Oerlikon pilot, full network operational within 18–24 months. Targets families, seniors, migrants and unemployed youth.

title: Oerlikon–Seebach Health Hub: Telemedicine, Mobile Clinic & Green Therapy for Kreis 11
description: Refurbish a ground-floor clinic at Bahnhof Oerlikon (Bahnhofplatz) as a multilingual primary-care and mental-health hub; deploy a weekly mobile clinic to Seebach (Seebacherplatz) and Affoltern; install telemedicine booths and AI triage kiosks at Bahnhof Oerlikon and Seebacherplatz; build a therapeutic community garden and outdoor rehabilitation circuit in MFO-Park; run monthly health fairs in cooperation with Hallenstadion. Targets seniors, migrants, families, chronically ill. Timeline: 3 months co-design, 9 months renovation/equipment, 6-month pilot — full roll-out in 18 months.

title: Oerlikon‑Messe Skills & Start‑Up Hub: Training, Makerspace, and Jobs for Kreis 11 Residents
description: Convert vacant commercial space beside Bahnhof Oerlikon into a public-run Skills & Start‑Up Hub adjacent to Messe Zürich and Hallenstadion. Offer apprenticeship bridging (ICT, green construction, hospitality), a makerspace (CNC, 3D printers, commercial kitchen), co-working for microbusinesses, and a digital job-matching platform. Target youth (16–30), long-term unemployed, migrants, and small businesses in Affoltern, Oerlikon and Seebach. Timeline: Phase 1 (0–12 months) renovate space and launch training; Phase 2 (12–36 months) expand pop-up retail on Schaffhauserstrasse and host annual job fair at Messe/Hallenstadion.

title: Seefeld Green Spine: Climate-Resilient Lakeside Wetland from Tiefenbrunnen Bahnhof to Zürichhorn
description: Transform the Mythenquai/Seefeldquai stretch (Bahnhof Tiefenbrunnen to Pavillon Le Corbusier/Zürichhorn) into a connected wetland promenade: floating reed islands, bioswales, raised boardwalks, native planting, stormwater retention tanks and water-quality sensors. Benefits: flood attenuation, cleaner lake water, biodiversity, accessible seating and learning nodes for schools. Implementation: design & permits (6–9 months), construction in phases (24 months) with Zürich city, Hafenbetrieb, and local NGOs. Targets residents, swimmers at Strandbad Tiefenbrunnen, schools and researchers; phased maintenance & education program year 3 onward.

title: Mühlebach–Weinegg Urban Orchard & Cool Corridor along Mühlebachstrasse and Weineggstrasse
description: Create pocket orchards, shade-tree corridors and pollinator strips on medians and plots along Mühlebachstrasse (between Seefeldquai and Bahnhof Tiefenbrunnen) and Weineggstrasse near the Seefeld promenade. Add 60 fruit trees, 20 pollinator beds, permeable paving, 6 smart misting/cooling nodes at bus stops, 10 solar-lit smart benches with USB and air sensors. Implementation: community co‑design (3 months), planting & infrastructure (9–12 months), stewardship program with local residents and schools. Targets families, seniors, commuters and local businesses; reduces heat, improves local food access and biodiversity.

title: Tiefenbrunnen Smart Mobility Hub at SBB plaza: e-fleet, cargo-bikes, repair workshop
description: Create an intermodal plaza directly outside SBB Tiefenbrunnen (Mythenquai/Tiefenbrunnenplatz) with 250 secure bike racks, 30 shared e-bikes, 10 community cargo e-bikes, sheltered bus/tram waiting, a staffed repair café/community workshop, 20 kW solar canopy, realtime ZVV timetable displays and unified contactless payments. Targets residents, commuters, seniors, local shops and families. Implementation: design 0–6 months, procurement 6–14 months, build and rollout 14–24 months. Governance: neighborhood coop + Stadt Zürich operations agreement.

title: Seefeld Mythenquai Car‑Lite Promenade: green tram-priority corridor and pop-up plazas
description: Transform Mythenquai (Seefeldquai/Zürichhorn to Strandbad Tiefenbrunnen) into a continuous car‑lite promenade: one dedicated green tram track with raised platforms for tram priority, widened protected bike lanes, rain gardens and 300 new trees, dynamic curbspace for deliveries, accessible ramps to lakeside, smart adaptive signals and seasonal car‑free festivals. Benefits families, older residents, commuters and local businesses. Timeline: feasibility & community design 0–9 months, phased construction 9–36 months, full activation by 36–48 months. Includes mobility education and pop-up markets.

title: Seefeld Green Corridor: Tiefenbrunnen–Hafen Riesbach Mobility & Play for Residents
description: Convert Seefeldstrasse (Tiefenbrunnen S-Bahn to Hafen Riesbach/Seefeldquai) into a car‑light Green Corridor: protected bike lanes and pedestrian plaza, micro‑mobility hub and cargo‑bike station at Tiefenbrunnen, rain gardens and permeable paving by Strandbad Tiefenbrunnen, smart LED lighting and air/noise sensors, plus a modular community pop‑up container at Hafen Riesbach for events, seniors’ meetups and child play. Targets families, commuters, seniors and local shops. Timeline: 6 months participatory design, 12 months phased construction, 6 months commissioning (24 months).

title: Mythenquai–Tiefenbrunnen Smart Clean Streets Hub for Seefeld Residents & Visitors
description: Pilot a smart-clean corridor along Mythenquai/Seefeldquai (Zürichhorn to Tiefenbrunnen Bahnhof) and Mühlebachstrasse: solar compacting bins with IoT fill/odour sensors, graffiti‑resistant bench and wall coatings, a free refill water station, and a local e‑cargo micro‑cleaning crew serving peak tram (Tiefenbrunnen) and lake events. Target groups: Seefeld residents, commuters, lake visitors, cafés. Timeline: 0–3 months procurement/installation, 3–6 months hire crew & launch volunteer clean days, 6–12 months optimize via public dashboard. Expected: faster response, 50% fewer overflows, less single‑use litter.

title: Seefeld–Mythenquai Waterfront Night‑Safe Network: Smart Lighting, Beacons, Lifesaving Stations
description: Install an integrated safety corridor along the lakeshore from Tiefenbrunnen SBB to Zürichhorn (Mythenquai/Seefeldquai): 25 solar adaptive LED lights (motion+crash-illumination), 12 smart emergency beacons with direct call to Stadtpolizei/ZVV, 8 heated lifebuoy+AED cabinets, shoreline water‑rescue sensors, multilingual QR instructions, and seasonal community lifeguard training. Partners: Stadtpolizei Zürich, SBB/Tiefenbrunnen station, Schweizerischer Rettungsverein. Timeline: 18 months (3m planning, 6m procurement, 6m install, 3m training/testing). Beneficiaries: residents, families, seniors, commuters, night workers and lake users in Kreis 8.

title: Zürichhorn Makers & Arts Hub for Seefeld Residents
description: Convert the Pavillon Le Corbusier courtyard and adjacent Seefeldquai storage into a year‑round community makerspace and micro‑gallery. Install digital labs (VR editing, 3D printers), woodworking and textile studios, an accessible rehearsal room, and a small outdoor amphitheatre facing the lake. Target groups: local youth, seniors, migrant communities, and independent artists. Implementation: retrofit existing service building, partner with Schule Seefeld and Kunstschaffende Riesbach, staff training and program launch in 18 months, weekly workshops, artist residencies and quarterly public showcases.

title: Riesbach Lake Culture Campus: Floating Stage & Studios at Hafen Riesbach
description: Create a cultural campus across Hafen Riesbach and Strandbad Tiefenbrunnen with a modular solar‑powered floating stage, containerized backstage studios and soundproof practice rooms, accessible lake ramps and a seasonal ‘Badi Kultur’ festival. Offer free school outreach, weekend family programming, artist residencies and livestreaming/AR guided performances along Seefeldquai and Utoquai. Implementation: build modular pontoons and container village, install tech and accessibility features, program development with local cultural groups; construction and pilot festival within 24 months.

title: Seefeld Makerspace & LakeLAB at Tiefenbrunnen: Youth Tech, Climate, Outdoor Learning for Kreis 8
description: Convert two rooms at Bahnhof Tiefenbrunnen and a moored classroom platform at Zürichhorn/Seefeldquai into a youth makerspace + LakeLAB. Target 6–18-year-olds (Schulhaus Seefeld, Mühlebach, newcomer families), offering 3D printers (x4), CNC, soldering benches, VR/AR, solar charging, and IoT water/air sensors along Seefeldquai to Strandbad Tiefenbrunnen. Timeline: 0–6 months planning/permits with Stadt Zürich Bildungsdepartement, 6–18 months renovation & equipment, 18–36 months program rollout with ETH/UZH student mentors, apprenticeships, bilingual courses and summer STEAM camps.

title: Zürichhorn Floating Sports Hub and All‑Season Badi Upgrade for Kreis 8 Residents
description: Install a modular floating sports platform anchored off Zürichhorn (between China Garden and Badi Tiefenbrunnen) and upgrade Badi Tiefenbrunnen changing rooms into an all‑season community sports centre. Improvements: floating zones for beach volleyball, SUP/kayak launch, climbing boulder, lifeguard/first‑aid station, solar lighting; refurbished accessible changing rooms, heated indoor training hall for winter, smart booking app and community coaching with local schools and clubs. Target groups: children, youth, seniors, disabled. Timeline: 6m design/permits, 12m construction/installation, 6m program rollout (24 months).

title: Seefeld Smart Street Sports Corridor: Parkour, Micro‑Fields, Outdoor Gym between Bellevue and Tiefenbrunnen
description: Convert portions of the Seefeldquai/Utoquai promenade (Bellevue tram stop down to Tiefenbrunnen SBB) into a continuous sports corridor: all‑weather 3x3 basketball and futsal micro‑fields at tram stops, a landscaped parkour trail by the China Garden entrance, calisthenics nodes near Seefeldstrasse, nighttime solar LED and sensor lighting, and a reservation/usage app with live occupancy. Targets youth, commuters, families and seniors. Implementation: 3 pilot sections in 12 months, full corridor in 24 months, run with schools, Jugendhaus and local clubs for programming.

title: Hafen Riesbach modular intergenerational housing with community hub and childcare
description: Transform the municipal parking area at Hafen Riesbach (adjacent to Seefeldquai, Chinese Garden and Strandbad Tiefenbrunnen) into ~40 energy‑efficient modular apartments (mix of 1–3 rooms), a ground‑floor community hub, an 8‑place subsidised childcare, rooftop garden/play and secure bicycle parking. Targets: young families, seniors, low‑income households and local artists; priority for Kreis 8 residents. Implementation: Year 1 planning/permits with Stadt Zürich and a Wohnbaugenossenschaft, Year 2 modular offsite construction and site works, Year 3 fit‑out, community move‑in. Features: Minergie‑P standard, PV, district heating tie‑in, smart building app and car‑share bay beside Bahnhof Tiefenbrunnen (≈300 m).

title: Hafen Riesbach Intergenerational Resilience Hub for Seefeld Seniors, Families and Migrants
description: Convert the unused pavilion area adjacent to Hafen Riesbach (by Strandbad Tiefenbrunnen and Seefeldquai promenade) into a solar-powered community hub offering a 30-place multilingual daycare, a 40-person seniors' day room with quiet zones, a community kitchen/food-sharing pantry, job/advice pop-ups, tool library and weekly skills-exchange. Include a digital booking/volunteer app, emergency cooling/warming room, bike repair station and monthly intergenerational events on the Zürichhorn lawn. Partners: City social services, local NGOs, 18-month rollout (6m planning, 12m build & staff training).

title: Seefeld Healthy Living Hub at Tiefenbrunnen for Seniors & Families
description: Modular community health centre on the Mythenquai promenade beside Badi Tiefenbrunnen / Tiefenbrunnen SBB: 2 telemedicine booths, nurse-led walk-in clinic, physiotherapy studio, weekly GP pop-ups, multilingual health navigators, and an 800m outdoor “active ageing” rehab trail with sensor-equipped benches and exercise stations toward Chinagarten. Targets older residents, families and commuters; partners with Stadt Zürich Gesundheitsamt and UZH student volunteers. Timeline: design 0–6 months, prefab build 6–15 months, 12-month pilot with outcome monitoring and scalable plan for other Kreise.

title: Zürichhorn Green Jobs & Innovation Hub: Training, Microenterprise, Electric Boats for Kreis 8 Residents
description: Transform the Hafen Riesbach boathouse and a modular pavilion at Zürichhorn/Seefeldquai into a Green Jobs & Innovation Hub offering vocational training (electric boat maintenance, renewable energy installation, hospitality & digital microbusiness), coworking/makerspace with CNC/3D printers, a local marketplace and a pilot fleet of 3 electric shuttle boats run by trainees. Target groups: unemployed residents, youth, migrants, local SMEs. Timeline: 6-month design, 18-month pilot training for 120 participants, full operation in Year 3; integrate smart booking with Tiefenbrunnen SBB and local NGOs.

title: Dolder–Adlisberg Climate Forest and Community Carbon Park for Hirslanden/Hottingen
description: Transform 2.5 ha of municipal woodland between Dolderbahn (Kurhausstrasse) and Adlisberg (near Dolder Sports) into a climate-resilient forest: 2,000 native trees, 5 community orchards, 3 stormwater retention basins, and a community biochar pilot. Target groups: Hottingen and Hirslanden residents, Hirslanden Klinik staff, local schools. Implementation: Phase 1 (0–6 months) survey and permit; Phase 2 (6–18 months) planting, retention basins, sensors; Phase 3 (18–30 months) biochar unit, educational programming. Integrate soil moisture and CO2 sensors with an app for volunteer coordination and long‑term monitoring.

title: Zoo–Rigiblick Green Corridor: Rain Gardens, Pollinator Bridge, and Zero‑Emission Mobility for Families
description: Create a 1.8 km green corridor from Zoo Zürich (Zürichbergstrasse) along Zürichbergstrasse to Rigiplatz and Rigiblick: continuous pollinator plantings, rain‑garden swales at tram and bus stops (Rigiplatz, Dolderbahn stops), 4 permeable mini‑plazas, 2 electric community cargo‑bike hubs, and solar-lit walking routes. Target groups: families, commuters, elderly. Timeline: design (0–6 months), construction (6–20 months), community programming and monitoring (20–36 months). Install air-quality and noise sensors and an open-data dashboard to measure biodiversity gains and modal shift away from cars.

title: Rigiplatz Green Mobility Hub: e-bikes, cargo-bikes and smart shelter for Hottingen & Fluntern
description: Create a multimodal hub at Rigiplatz (adjacent to the Rigiblick theatre and Rigiplatz bus stop) with 30 public e-bikes, 12 community cargo-bikes, sheltered solar charging canopies, secure bike parking and an integrated app for bookings and ZVV ticket linking. Target groups: seniors, families, Zoo Zürich visitors, Hirslanden hospital staff and local commuters. Implementation: pilot service, community training and reduced fares in months 1–12; full rollout and IoT monitoring months 13–18.

title: Zürichberg Ridge e‑Way: protected Fluntern–Dolder cycle-pedestrian corridor with smart systems
description: Build a protected active-transport corridor from Zoo Zürich (Fluntern) along Zürichbergstrasse to Dolderbahn/Dolderstrasse, linking Rigiplatz and Hirslanden. Works include segregated, gently graded cycle lanes, raised crossings, heated sections on steep ramps, secure bike parking at Dolderbahn and Hirslanden hospital, solar LED adaptive lighting, air-quality sensors and 8 e-charging stations. Timeline: planning & permits 6–12 months, phased construction 18–30 months. Benefits commuters, schoolchildren, elderly residents and reduces short car trips across Kreis 7.

title: Zürichberg Green Promenade: step‑free link from Zoo Zürich to Rigiblick for Kreis 7 residents
description: Create a 1.2 km accessible green promenade along Zürichbergstrasse (between Zollikerstrasse and Dolderstrasse) linking Zoo Zürich main entrance, Rigiblick theatre forecourt and the Dolderbahn upper area. Works: widen and de‑steepen paths, add universal ramps/elevators at two steep nodes, smart LED motion lighting, air‑quality sensors and public Wi‑Fi, two e‑cargo/e‑bike hubs (Zoo and Rigiblick), pocket plazas with community orchard and pollinator meadow, outdoor class/fitness modules for schools and seniors. Targets families, elderly, commuters and local shops. Timeline: planning 6 months, construction 24 months, community activation ongoing.

title: Zürichberg–Dolder Smart Clean Corridors: Sensor Bins, Green Lanes, Community Hubs
description: Transform Zürichbergstrasse, Dolderstrasse, the Zoo Zürich plaza and Rigiblick stop with 30 solar-powered sensor bins (compacting, fill alerts), 6 rain-gardens/bioretention strips to trap litter and storm runoff, 3 community micro-hubs for sorting/compost drop-off, and an e-bike rapid-response cleaning team. Target groups: residents (Hottingen/Fluntern/Hirslanden), Zoo visitors, Dolderbahn passengers and local schools (Primarschule Hottingen). Timeline: 3 months planning + community workshops, 9 months phased installation, 12-month pilot with real-time cleanliness map integrated into the Stadt Zürich app.

title: Smart Safe‑Routes Network for Dolder–Zoo–Witikon: lighting, hubs, patrols for residents
description: Install adaptive LED streetlighting, 8 solar emergency-call hubs with direct Stadtpolizei link and CCTV, and two electric community patrols along Dolderstrasse (Römerhof–Dolder), Zürich Zoo main entrance/walking paths and Witikon village centre (Dorfplatz and nearby bus stops). Target groups: seniors, families, evening commuters and visitors. Timeline: 0–6 months community design and sensor siting, 6–18 months infrastructure and hub installation, 18–24 months pilot patrols and evaluation. Measures: reduced night incidents, faster response times, safety workshops and youth ambassador program.

title: Zürichberg Cultural Green Corridor: Night Arts between Museum Rietberg and Zoo Zürich
description: Transform the stretch along Zürichbergstrasse between Museum Rietberg (Rieterpark) and Zoo Zürich (Rehalp/Dolderbahn area) into a year‑round cultural green corridor: smart LED/night lighting, multilingual audio‑tours, 3 pop‑up performance nodes, free public Wi‑Fi, interactive art installations co‑created with local schools and Rietberg, and weekend evening programming for families and seniors. Implementation: planning 3 months, pilot 6 months at Rieterpark entrance, full rollout 12–18 months. Targets: families, seniors, commuters, tourists; partners: Museum Rietberg, Zoo Zürich, Kreis 7 schools.

title: Witikon Makerspace & Outdoor Stage at Witikerplatz for Youth, Artists, Schools
description: Convert the vacant municipal building at Witikon village centre (Witikerplatz, by the Witikon bus stop) into a 1,000–1,500 m² cultural makerspace with rehearsal rooms, soundproof studios, digital media/VR lab, gallery, and subsidised artist studios plus a refurbished outdoor stage on the adjacent plaza. Programming: youth mentorship, refugee integration arts, school residencies with Museum Rietberg, evening community nights. Timeline: design 6 months, renovation 12–18 months, opening in 24 months. Targets: youth 14–30, local artists, schools, seniors.

title: Kreis 7 Youth Innovation & Nature Lab at Rigiblick – STEAM & Zoo Partnership for 10–18s
description: Convert the former Rigiblick community hall (near Rigiblickbahn stop) into a youth STEAM & Nature Lab serving 10–18-year-olds from Fluntern, Hottingen and Hirslanden. Equip maker space (3D printers, CNC, AR/VR, woodworking), classroom, outdoor learning courtyard linking guided modules with Zoo Zürich and Zürichberg Park biodiversity trails. Run coding, robotics, apprenticeship-prep, multilingual tutoring, and a solar-powered mobile FabLab bus serving Dolderbahn, Hottingen and Wollishofen schools. Timeline: 6 months community co-design, 12 months renovation/equipment, program launch at month 18; three-year pilot with annual evaluation. Partners: Zoo Zürich, Kantonsschule, Berufsbildungszentrum.

title: Dolder Active Hub: Smart Outdoor Sports Campus by Dolderbahn for All Ages
description: Install a multifunctional outdoor sports campus next to Dolderbahn/Dolder Sportspark (Dolderstrasse): 200m pump track, floodlit all-weather multisport court, accessible outdoor gym, 6m boulder wall, parkour line and solar LED path. Add IoT usage sensors, app booking, and live occupancy boards at Dolderbahn stop. Target: families, youth clubs (e.g. local schools & FC Hottingen partners), seniors and wheelchair users. Timeline: 4 months design/permits, 8 months construction, 4 months community programme setup (16 months). Includes coaching subsidies, maintenance fund, and partnership with Dolder Sport facilities.

title: Fluntern Seasonal Ice Rink & Summer Splash Park at Zoo Zürich Entrance
description: Create a modular, climate-friendly seasonal facility on the open lot by the Zoo Zürich entrance on Zürichbergstrasse: refrigerated 30x15m ice rink in winter, convertible to a shallow splash/play pool and inline-skate surface in summer, plus changing rooms, heated community lounge and equipment rental. Use heat-recovery to warm nearby community spaces and Schulen Fluntern teaching areas. Target: families, school groups, seniors, neighbourhood sports clubs. Timeline: 6 months planning, 12 months build-and-test; seasonal operation with school-programmes and learn-to-skate/swim subsidies.

title: Dolder–Witikon Intergenerational Mobility & Care Hub for Seniors and Families
description: Convert a municipal space near Dolderbahn station (Fluntern) into a staffed community hub linking Dolderbahn, Zürich Zoo entrance, Klinik Hirslanden and Witikonplatz. Offer an e-bike library (30 e-bikes), on‑demand electric minibus service, a communal kitchen, telemedicine booth, multilingual outreach, digital booking app and smart benches with Wi‑Fi. Target groups: older residents, families, caregivers, and young volunteers. Timeline: 6 months co‑design with neighbourhood, 12 months build/procurement, 6 months pilot service, ongoing community governance.

title: Dolder–Rigiblick Active Health Hub: Community Care & Tele‑Rehab for Kreis 7 Seniors
description: Convert underused community rooms near Rigiblick (Rigiblickstrasse) and a satellite space by Dolderbahn Rehalp into an integrated Active Health Hub: nurse‑led primary care, weekly geriatric day‑clinic, mental‑health drop‑in, telemedicine pods linked to Universitätsspital Zürich, and a 1.8 km smart ‘Active Ageing Trail’ along Dolderstrasse with sensor‑equipped exercise nodes, benches and accessible wayfinding. Add a mobile health bus serving Witikon Dorf and Hottingen outreach. Target groups: 65+, chronic patients, carers. Timeline: 6 months planning, 12 months build, 18‑month pilot and evaluation.

title: Fluntern–Dolder Green Jobs Hub near Zoo Zürich for youth, migrants, seniors
description: Repurpose an underused municipal building adjacent to Zürich Zoo (Fluntern) / Dolderbahn area into a 1,200 m² Green Jobs Hub. Deliverers: city, vocational schools, NGOs. Target groups: 60 local trainees annually (16–30 unemployed youth, migrants, returning parents, 50+ mentors). Facilities: makerspace (wood/metal/textiles), e‑bike repair lab, solar-install training array on the roof, 8 co‑work desks and 3 micro-retail pop-up units facing the Dolderstrasse pedestrian route. Timeline: 6 months planning, 12 months fit-out, 12 months pilot training + quarterly repair markets at zoo plaza. Outcome: 40 certified placements/year and new local social enterprises.

title: Zürich Urban Cooling Forest and Green Roof Network — schools to lake for all residents
description: Transform 5‑year programme to cool and green Zürich: plant 10,000 street trees and install 300 green roofs (≈40,000 m²) on public buildings including Zürich HB concourse, Stadthausquai offices, 60 municipal schools, Letzigrund and Sihlcity. Create bioswales and tree trenches along Bahnhofstrasse, Limmatquai, Bellevue–Bürkliplatz and the Sihl river, linking Uetliberg trails to the Lake Zurich promenade. Deploy soil‑moisture and heat sensors, an open-data dashboard and a citizen 'Adopt‑a‑Tree' volunteer maintenance network. Timeline: Year 1 pilots (HB, Bellevue, 10 schools); Years 2–5 citywide rollout.

title: City-wide Solar Canopy and Rainwater Microgrid on Tram Stops and Public Roofs
description: Five-year citywide install of solar canopies and rain-harvest microgrids: PV canopies on 300 high-traffic tram and bus stops (Zürich HB, Paradeplatz, Bürkliplatz, Bellevue) and 60 municipal roofs (schools, Letzigrund, Sihlcity). Add 2 MWh distributed battery storage, 400 m³ rainwater tanks for street cleaning and tree irrigation, and smart energy management with open API and community energy credits. Phasing: pilot on Line 4/6 corridor and HB Year 1; scale Years 2–6. Benefits: lower grid peaks, public EV charging, cheaper power for community centres and climate resilience.

title: Smart Mobility Hubs across Zürich: Hauptbahnhof, Bellevue, Oerlikon, Altstetten, Enge
description: Create 15 city-wide Smart Mobility Hubs (pilot: Hauptbahnhof, Oerlikon, Bellevue) at major nodes: Bahnhofplatz/Hauptbahnhof, Bürkliplatz/Bahnhofstrasse, Bellevue, Sihlcity, Hardbrücke, Oerlikon, Altstetten, Wipkingen, Seefeld, Höngg +5. Each hub provides secure 200-bike parking (incl. 50 e‑bike/cargo docks), cargo-bike rental, parcel lockers, microrepair workshop, real-time ZVV displays, solar canopies and multilingual kiosks. Targets commuters, parents, delivery SMEs and seniors. Timeline: 12‑month 3‑site pilot, city roll‑out over 36 months with co‑design and procurement phases.

title: NightLink 24/7 Electric Shuttles Connecting Hbf, Flughafen, Langstrasse, Oerlikon, Altstetten
description: Launch NightLink: 24/7 electric on‑demand shuttles (start 10 vehicles) plus three fixed-night corridors with priority lanes on Sihlquai, Langstrasse/Helvetiaplatz and Hardbrücke. Stops include Hauptbahnhof, Langstrasse, Sihlcity, Enge, Hardbrücke, Oerlikon, Flughafen (Zürich Airport connection) and Altstetten. Integrated with ZVV fares, bookable by app/SMS, wheelchair‑accessible, with CCTV, high‑visibility lighting and trained personnel. Targets shift workers, nightlife users, students, tourists and airport staff. Timeline: 18‑month pilot, scale to 30 vehicles and 3 full lines within 3 years.

title: City-wide Neighbourhood Hubs Network: vacant shops from Bahnhofstrasse to Wipkingen for families, startups
description: Convert vacant ground-floor shops (Bahnhofstrasse/Paradeplatz, Langstrasse 77, Wipkingenplatz, Oerlikon Bahnhofplatz, Altstetten Zentrum) into modular Neighbourhood Hubs offering pop-up daycare (12–20 slots), coworking (10–30 desks), maker labs, language cafés, micro-health consultation rooms, bike repair and free Wi‑Fi. Pilot 5 sites in 12 months (3-month planning), citywide roll-out across all districts in 36 months. Targets families, seniors, refugees, students and entrepreneurs. Partners: City of Zürich, property owners, NGOs, ETH/ZHdK; includes energy retrofits, solar panels and a smart booking app.

title: City-wide Smart Clean Streets Network: Solar-Compacting Bins & Rapid E-bike Teams (Bahnhofstrasse–Langstrasse)
description: Deploy a city-wide IoT cleaning system focused on Bahnhofstrasse, Zürich HB, Langstrasse, Bellevue, Bürkliplatz, Limmatquai, Seefeld and Uetliberg trailheads. Install 150 solar-compacting sensor bins, 300 cigarette-butt receptacles, 4 electric micro-sweepers and 8 rapid-response e-bike cleaning teams for nightlife/market hours. Integrate sensors into a public dashboard and VBZ dispatch; launch a neighbourhood reporting app with volunteer cleanups and small rewards. Pilot 12 months (Q1 2026–Q4 2026) in Hauptbahnhof–Langstrasse, then phased city-wide rollout 2027–2029 with operator training and maintenance plan.

title: City-wide Smart Safety Network across Bahnhofstrasse–Langstrasse–Oerlikon for residents
description: Install 350 solar-powered smart LED poles with motion-sensor lighting, emergency call buttons, noise-event detection, and edge-processed cameras at Bahnhofstrasse (Bürkliplatz–Hauptbahnhof), Langstrasse corridor (Helvetiaplatz–Badenerstrasse), Oerlikon Bahnhof/Letzigrund, Sihlquai and Platzspitz. Integrate with Stadtpolizei Zürich dispatch and a multilingual community app for alerts and anonymous reports; train 60 community safety ambassadors (night workers, students, elderly volunteers). Pilot 6 months on Bahnhofstrasse/Langstrasse, full city rollout 24 months. Privacy-first design: no continuous cloud video, encrypted incident clips released only to authorities.

title: Limmat Floating Stages: Free Performances from Bürkliplatz to Technopark for All Zürich
description: Install six modular floating stages moored at Bürkliplatz, Bellevue (Quaibrücke), Münsterbrücke, Central (Limmatquai), Schiffbau (Escher-Wyss-Platz) and Technopark. Offer weekly free concerts, theatre, youth workshops and multilingual family programming. Improvements: accessible ramps, power, lighting, PA, artist cabins, ZVV-accessible schedules. Target groups: families, seniors, youth, migrants, neighbourhood associations. Timeline: 6 months design & permits with Hafenbetrieb, 9 months build, first 12-month pilot (spring–autumn seasons) with evaluation and seasonal festival finale at Bürkliplatz.

title: KulturPass Zürich: City-Wide Digital Card and AR Tours for Residents (Kunsthaus–Grossmünster)
description: Create a subsidised KulturPass (NFC card + app) giving residents reduced/free entry to Kunsthaus, Opernhaus, Rietberg, Schauspielhaus, Volkshaus and community spaces; includes AR location-based guided stories at Grossmünster, Lindenhof, Bahnhofstrasse, Niederdorf and Brunau Park. Target groups: low-income households, students, seniors, new residents. Improvements: multilingual content, offline maps, museum scheduling, outreach via libraries and Stadthaus. Timeline: 3 months procurement, 9 months tech & content build with ETH/ZHAW and cultural partners, 6-month city-wide pilot and onboarding program.

title: City-wide Youth STEAM & Apprenticeship Hubs at Hauptbahnhof–Zentralbibliothek–Oerlikon for 10–25-year-olds
description: Create six fixed Youth STEAM & career hubs (Zentralbibliothek, Hauptbahnhof concourse room, Technopark/Kreis 5, Oerlikon community hall near Oerlikon Station, Seebach Kulturzentrum, Rote Fabrik annex) plus four mobile maker-trams serving Bürkliplatz, Bahnhofstrasse, Helvetiaplatz and Letzigrund. Equip with 3D printers, CNC, VR labs, sound studio, career counselling and digital badge system; target 10–25-year-olds (incl. apprentices, NEETs, refugees). Timeline: 6‑month pilot (2 hubs), 18‑month citywide rollout, 6‑month evaluation. Delivered with ETH/UZH outreach, Berufsbildung Zürich and Zentralbibliothek partnerships.

title: Smart Multi-Sport Hubs at Letzigrund, Zürichhorn, Oerlikon — Free, Inclusive Fitness for All
description: Build 8 outdoor, all-ages multi-sport hubs (Letzigrund stadium entrance, Zürichhorn lakeside near Chinagarten, Oerlikon/Messeplatz, Wipkingen near Wipkingenbrücke, Albisrieden Soodstrasse, Irchelpark, Seefeld/Bellerivestrasse, Hönggerberg). Each hub: modular futsal/basketball court, calisthenics, accessible fitness equipment, solar LED floodlights, free Wi‑Fi, sensor counters and a booking/coach app. Weekly free classes for youth, seniors, disabled athletes. Pilot at Letzigrund in 6 months, roll-out citywide within 24 months, staffed via local clubs and sports office partnerships.

title: Zurich Smart 42km Sports Circuit from Hauptbahnhof to Letzigrund — Training, Events for Everyone
description: Create a marked 42 km loop linking Hauptbahnhof → Bürkliplatz → Utoquai → Zürichhorn → Tiefenbrunnen → Käferberg → Irchelpark → Oerlikon → Letzigrund. Install smart stations every 2–3 km with water, solar lighting, emergency call, timing sensors and AR audio routes in German/English. Resurface key stretches, upgrade crossings at Quaibrücke and Bahnhofstrasse, add wheelchair-accessible segments. Pilot 10 km from Hauptbahnhof to Zürichhorn in 12 months, full circuit phased over 36 months, tied to Zurich Marathon, schools and community running/walking programmes.

title: Modular Affordable Housing Hubs at Hauptbahnhof, Oerlikon, Letten for Families, Seniors, Key Workers
description: Convert underused municipal plots and partner sites into three modular, energy-positive housing hubs: Hauptbahnhof (Sihlquai parking podium by Bahnhofplatz/Hardbrücke), Oerlikon (Leutschenbach/Oerlikon Bahnhof lot) and Letten riverside (near Limmatquai). Deliver 300 mixed units (150 family, 90 single, 60 senior-accessible) with communal kitchens, on-site childcare, co-working, medical outreach, green roofs, photovoltaic + heat-pump, 600 bike spaces and integrated VBZ mobility passes. Managed by Wohnbaugenossenschaften with priority for low-income households, key workers and artists. Timeline: 0–6m design/permits, 6–18m retrofit/modular build, 18–36m occupancy.

title: Zürich Solidarity Hubs Network (Hauptbahnhof→Oerlikon→Helvetiaplatz): Community Services for Seniors, Migrants, Youth
description: Create a city-wide network of 10 staffed Solidarity Hubs at existing sites (Bahnhofplatz/Hauptbahnhof, Bürkliplatz, Helvetiaplatz, Langstrasse, Oerlikon station, Altstetten/Sihlcity, Rote Fabrik, Seefeld, GZ Wipkingen, GZ Höngg) plus a mobile Solidarity Bus visiting Letzigrund and Aussersihl. Offer multilingual counselling, legal/administrative aid, digital inclusion labs, community kitchens, low-threshold childcare, warming spaces, and mental-health drop-ins. Integrate a single app/real-time capacity map, free Wi‑Fi, tablet translators and unified case management. Timeline: Year 1 pilot four hubs + bus; Year 2 expand to 10; Year 3 full operations and evaluation.

title: 24/7 Community Health Micro‑Hubs at Hauptbahnhof, Bellevue, Oerlikon for All Zürich Residents
description: Install 12 staffed micro‑clinics and 30 telemedicine booths at key nodes (Bahnhofplatz/Hauptbahnhof, Sechseläutenplatz/Bellevue, Oerlikon Bahnhofplatz, Altstetten Bahnhofplatz, Triemli Spitalplatz, Bürkliplatz, Letzigraben/Wipkingen, Enge Bahnhof, Rote Fabrik area, Letzigrund Stadium, Mythenquai, Irchel Campus). Services: nurse triage, vaccinations, chronic care checks (BP, glucose, HbA1c point‑of‑care), mental‑health first aid, multilingual outreach (DE/EN/FR/IT/AL), integration with Universitätsspital Zürich telemedicine and city health portal, mobile vans for parks (Platzspitz, Seefeld). Timeline: 6‑month design, 12‑month pilot (3 sites), full roll‑out by 24 months.

title: Mythenquai–Wollishofen Green Corridor: Pollinators, Flood Resilience & Active Routes
description: Transform Mythenquai promenade via Enge Bahnhof to Bahnhof Wollishofen along Seestrasse into a 2.8 km green corridor: native pollinator meadows, bioswales and permeable paving at tram stops, raised play-gardens for children, benches for seniors, LED wayfinding and soil-moisture sensors. Targets: residents, commuters, local primary schools (Enge/Wollishofen), elderly. Phases: 0–6m design & permits; 6–18m construction (bioswales, planting); 18–24m community planting & monitoring. Benefits: reduce runoff to Lake Zürich, increase biodiversity, safer car-free active routes, school environmental curriculum.

title: Wollishofen Floating Solar-Biodiversity Pier at Strandbad for Community Energy & Education
description: Install a 180–220 kWp floating solar pier with modular reed islands, fish & bird habitat, and a public boardwalk off Strandbad Wollishofen/Schiffstation. Includes real-time environmental sensors with a public dashboard, outdoor classroom docks for local schools and Rietberg Museum outreach, and a microgrid to power the Strandbad and nearby community buildings. Phases: 0–9m feasibility & permits (ZH Gewässeramt), 9–24m construction, 24–36m commissioning & education rollout. Targets residents, swimmers, students and small businesses; reduces shoreline erosion and supplies ~15% local energy demand.

title: Active Mobility Hubs at Bahnhof Enge, Mythenquai, Wollishofen for Residents
description: Create three integrated mobility hubs at Bahnhof Enge, Strandbad Mythenquai (near Mythenquai promenade) and Wollishofen Bahnhof: 200 secure long‑term bike spaces, cargo‑bike lending library, 12 e‑bike charging points, staffed weekly repair pop‑ups, covered waiting areas with real‑time VBZ/SBB displays and local wayfinding to Rote Fabrik. Phased rollout: 3‑month design, 6‑month pilot at Enge, full network live within 12 months. Targets commuters, families, seniors, local shops; reduces car trips and makes first/last mile seamless with tech and community-run maintenance.

title: Seestrasse Low‑Emission Transit Boulevard: Priority E‑Bus/Tram & Protected Lanes (Enge–Wollishofen)
description: Transform Seestrasse between Bahnhof Enge, Strandbad Mythenquai and Wollishofen Bahnhof into a low‑emission transit corridor: centre‑running dedicated e‑bus/tram lanes with raised boarding islands, continuous protected two‑way cycle track, widened lakeside pedestrian verges, bioswale rain gardens, adaptive signal priority integrated with VBZ, and dynamic curb zones for deliveries. Includes stop upgrades (Wollishofen Bahnhof, Mythenquai), community consultation and a 6‑month car‑light weekend pilot. Timeline: 6–12 months planning, 24–36 months construction. Benefits commuters, lake visitors, businesses and schoolchildren, cutting emissions and improving safety.

title: Mythenquai Green Corridor: Lakeside Mobility and Community Hubs for Enge–Wollishofen Residents
description: Transform Mythenquai between Seebad Enge and Bahnhof Wollishofen into a resilient green corridor: raised protected cycle lane, widened accessible lakeside promenade, two pocket plazas (near Seebad Enge and Wollishofen Dorfkern), five solar pergolas with e-bike charging, sensor-controlled lighting and air-quality monitoring, and a converted room at Bahnhof Wollishofen as a community workshop/market. Targets families, seniors, commuters, and local businesses. Timeline: 3-month design & community co-creation, 9-month pilot (protected lane, plaza, sensors), 12-month full build and programming.

title: Smart Clean Corridor: Seestrasse–Enge–Mythenquai Sensors, Robots & Community Hubs
description: Transform Seestrasse (Zürich Enge Bahnhof) to Strandbad Mythenquai with 18 solar compacting smart bins, 4 micro-recycling stations at Mythenquai and Wollishofen Bahnhof, two autonomous electric night sweepers for the promenade, and a cargo-bike vacuum for daytime hotspots. Add a mobile app for real-time fill/status reporting, monthly community 'Clean Sundays' with local businesses, and school outreach. Timeline: 18 months (3m design, 3m procurement, 6m install/training, 6m pilot & evaluation). Benefits residents, commuters, lake visitors and local shops; operated with Stadt Zürich cleaning partners.

title: Smart Safe Night Network: Enge–Wollishofen lighting, SOS points & community hosts
description: Install 30 adaptive LED nodes, 4 emergency call pillars (direct link to Stadtpolizei), and two lake-rescue stations along Seestrasse/Mythenquai between Bahnhof Enge, Seebad Enge, Rote Fabrik and Bahnhof Wollishofen. Add privacy-respecting motion sensors (no CCTV), a neighbourhood SOS/safe-route app integration, and train a 20-person ‘Safety Host’ volunteer corps via Quartierverein Enge/Wollishofen with Stadtpolizei instruction. Targets commuters, night workers, families, elderly and cyclists. Timeline: 2 months planning, 12 months installation & training, 4 months pilot evaluation with public reporting.

title: Mythenquai–Enge Floating Cultural Promenade: Lake Stages & Pop‑up Galleries
description: Install a modular floating promenade and two adaptable stages on the Mythenquai shoreline between Bahnhof Enge and Strandbad Enge. Target groups: families, local artists, seniors, commuters. Improvements: accessible gangways, modular stages for concerts/film, nightly curated pop‑up galleries, low‑impact LED lighting, shore power, free public Wi‑Fi and an AR audio tour app about Enge history. Implementation: design 4–6 months, fabrication & permits 6–9 months, pilot festival in summer (month 12–14). Operated seasonally by Stadt Zürich Kultur with resident artist weeks.

title: Wollishofen Community Arts Hub at Bahnhof Wollishofen: Makerspace, Black‑Box Theatre
description: Convert vacant municipal floors or adjacent former depot near Bahnhof Wollishofen into a subsidised cultural hub. Target groups: youth, migrants, emerging artists, schools. Specifics: 3 artist studios, digital fab lab (3D printer, laser cutter), 80‑seat black‑box theatre with livestream capability, rehearsal rooms, multilingual community classes, rooftop solar and rainwater for workshops. Timeline: feasibility & community design 3–4 months, renovation 10–14 months, program launch month 15 with school partnerships and open studio nights every fortnight.

title: Kreis 2 Youth Innovation Campus: Bahnhof Enge–Wollishofen Makerspace for 12–18-year-olds
description: Transform vacant rooms at Bahnhof Enge and the boathouse at Wollishofen Hafen into a linked Youth Innovation Campus. Target 10–18-year-olds from Primarschule Enge, Sekundarschule Wollishofen and Leimbach, offering a digital fabrication lab (3D printers, CNC, laser), robotics/VR suites, sound studio, multilingual tutoring, evening coding clubs and a subsidised 'Maker-Mob' van serving Leimbach. Partner with ETH and ZHdK student mentors and local firms. Timeline: 6‑month pilot in Bahnhof Enge, full Wollishofen boathouse renovation, mobile lab and smart booking app live within 24 months.

title: Floating Lake Sports Hub at Mythenquai by Bahnhof Enge
description: Build a 50×30m anchored floating sports platform at Mythenquai (lakefront beside Bahnhof Enge) with swim docks, accessible ramp, SUP/kayak launch, beach-volleyball court, bouldering wall, solar lighting and water-quality sensors. Add a lifeguard station, integrated booking/safety app and free school and youth programmes co-run with local clubs. Timeline: 6 months design, 12 months permitting, 8 months construction. Targets families, students, water-sport clubs and seniors; connects to Seestrasse promenade and Enge rail stop for easy access.

title: Wollishofen All-Weather Community Sports Campus at Bahnhof Wollishofen
description: Convert the surface parking at Bahnhof Wollishofen / Wollishofen Bahnhofplatz (Seestrasse) into a modular sports campus with three indoor courts (retractable roof), rooftop 5-a-side artificial turf, climbing wall, fitness studio, changing rooms, solar canopy and EV chargers. Smart booking prioritises Primarschule Wollishofen, youth leagues and seniors’ slots; VBZ stop integration ensures transit access. Timeline: 4 months co-design, 10 months permits, 12 months construction. Serves schools, local clubs, families, commuters and creates year-round training space in Kreis 2.

title: Modular mixed‑income co‑housing at Wollishofen Güterbahnhof for families & seniors
description: Convert the former Güterbahnhof Wollishofen and adjacent Enge Bahnhof surface parking into 120 modular apartments (40% capped‑rent), intergenerational common rooms, 10‑place onsite childcare, rooftop PV (≈200 kWp) and community gardens. Add a mobility hub with 100 secure bike spaces and 20 EV chargers, smart meters and building‑energy management (pilot with ZHAW/ETH). Target groups: low‑income households, young families, seniors, local artists. Timeline: 6 months community design, 12 months permits & funding, 18–24 months phased modular construction and occupancy.

title: Enge–Wollishofen Lakefront Community Hub for Seniors, Families and Creatives at Mythenquai
description: Transform the vacant lakeside plot by Rote Fabrik/Strandbad Mythenquai (walking distance from Wollishofen and Enge Bahnhof) into 8 solar-paneled modular units: 20 co‑working desks, a community kitchen, a 10‑place drop‑in childcare, repair café, and flexible room for language cafés and senior digital-literacy classes. Target groups: seniors, low-income families, refugees, students, local artists. Run by local NGOs with Stadt Zürich permits, partner with Rote Fabrik and schools. Timeline: 3 months planning, 3 months permits, 6 months build, launch month 13 with phased programming and a booking app.

title: Kreis 2 Community Health Hub + Telemedicine Kiosks at Bahnhof Enge, Wollishofen, Leimbach (Elderly & Families)
description: Convert Bahnhof Enge ground-floor space into a nurse-led Community Health Hub and install three smart telemedicine kiosks (Bahnhof Enge concourse, Wollishofen Dorfplatz by Seestrasse near the Strandbad area, Leimbach Park entrance). Add a weekly mobile clinic van on Seestrasse for homebound seniors. Services: triage, physiotherapy groups, mental-health counselling, social prescribing (guided park walks), multilingual community health workers, and an app linking bookings to USZ. Implementation: design 3 months, retrofit & kiosks 9 months, hire/train 6 months — full operation by month 18. Beneficiaries: elderly, commuters, families, migrants in Kreis 2.

title: Mythenquai–Bahnhof Enge GreenTech & Jobs Hub for Youth, Migrants, Local SMEs
description: Create a 24‑month GreenTech & Microenterprise Hub: retrofit vacant ground-floor space at Bahnhof Enge and a linked floating annex anchored at Mythenquai/Hafen Wollishofen. Offer 12 co‑work desks, 3 maker bays, IoT & solar labs, e-bike repair station, and a staffed job‑matching desk. Target 18–55 unemployed youth, migrants, parents returning to work, and local SMEs. Deliver apprenticeships with ZSG, local hotels, Rote Fabrik and ETH/UZH internships; integrate a live job dashboard tied to Stadt Zürich employment services. Timeline: 6 months planning, 12 months build/pilot, 6 months scale/evaluate.
